paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学的行为经济学家尤金·迪曼特表示，这项研究为人类在没有后果的情况下如何表现提供了一些敏锐的见解。 “但这不是世界运转的方式。”他的工作表明，要真正理解社会传染和暴民的出现，研究人员必须考虑社会力量，例如惩罚和社会规范，这些力量往往会控制行为。

paras.en: To Molleman, though, the study’s insights into individual behaviors are key. This pared-down experiment shows how just a few bad actors can cause entire groups to spiral out of control. Such findings could underpin everything from collective speeding to peaceful protests that turn violent, he says. “This is fundamental science … Obviously reality is way more complex.”
paras.zh: 不过，对于莫勒曼来说，这项研究对个人行为的洞察是关键。这个简化的实验表明，仅仅几个坏人就可以导致整个群体失控。他说，这些发现可以为从集体超速到演变为暴力的和平抗议等一切行为提供依据。 “这是基础科学……显然现实要复杂得多。”

articles.title: What can minerals tell us about Earth’s past? This geologist is finding out
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: The minute Gabriela Farfan stepped into a small natural history museum in Madison, Wis., where she grew up, she knew she wanted to work with minerals. Farfan remembers seeing all different shapes and colors and being enthralled. “From that point forward, I knew I wanted to become a geologist someday,” she says.
paras.zh: 加布里埃拉·法尔凡 (Gabriela Farfan) 踏入她长大的威斯康星州麦迪逊市的一家小型自然历史博物馆的那一刻，她就知道自己想从事矿物研究。法尔凡记得看到各种不同的形状和颜色并被迷住了。 “从那时起，我就知道有一天我想成为一名地质学家，”她说。

paras.en: Farfan is now living her teenage dream as the curator of gems and minerals at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. Her specialty is biomineralization — how organisms build skeletons, corals, pearls and shells. Farfan hopes to answer questions about how they form and what stories they tell by studying crystal structures and the chemistry of minerals.
paras.zh: Farfan 现在实现了她青少年时期的梦想，成为华盛顿特区史密森尼国家自然历史博物馆的宝石和矿物馆长。她的专长是生物矿化——生物体如何构建骨骼、珊瑚、珍珠和贝壳。法尔凡希望通过研究晶体结构和矿物化学来回答有关它们如何形成以及它们讲述什么故事的问题。

paras.en: These days, she investigates signals trapped within minerals. Corals, for example, build layers of calcium carbonate mineral over time, trapping chemical signatures from the ocean. The data tell all kinds of stories — about stress, disease outbreaks and changes to ocean temperature and sea level. Farfan unlocks those tales using X-ray and Raman spectroscopies, bouncing beams off samples to see what they can tell us.
paras.zh: 这些天，她研究了矿物中捕获的信号。例如，随着时间的推移，珊瑚会形成一层层碳酸钙矿物，捕获来自海洋的化学特征。这些数据讲述了各种各样的故事——关于压力、疾病爆发以及海洋温度和海平面的变化。 Farfan 使用 X 射线和拉曼光谱解开这些故事，从样本上反射光束，看看它们能告诉我们什么。

paras.en: She hopes museum visitors will remember that the sparkly gemstones, the ones that first enamored her, are just as natural as the plants and bones in other exhibits. “Minerals are actual natural history objects,” Farfan says. “Those are actually formed by Mother Nature and it’s spectacular.”
paras.zh: 她希望博物馆参观者能够记住，最初让她着迷的闪闪发光的宝石与其他展品中的植物和骨头一样天然。 “矿物是真正的自然历史物体，”法尔凡说。 “这些实际上是由大自然形成的，非常壮观。”

articles.title: This ‘living drug’ could change the course of autoimmune disease
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Two months before the treatment that would change Lynn Montgomery-Haga’s life, she could barely walk down a hallway.
paras.zh: 在接受改变林恩·蒙哥马利-哈加生活的治疗之前两个月，她几乎无法在走廊上行走。

paras.en: In a test at the University of Colorado Anschutz, Montgomery-Haga struggled to walk 25 feet, often reaching out to the walls for support. Usually, the 49-year-old relied on her walker or wheelchair. “She had a very stiff, hesitant gait,” says Montgomery-Haga’s neurologist, Amanda Piquet.
paras.zh: 在科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校进行的一次测试中，蒙哥马利-哈加很难行走 25 英尺，经常伸手到墙上寻求支撑。这位 49 岁的女士通常依靠助行器或轮椅出行。 “她的步态非常僵硬、犹豫，”蒙哥马利-哈加的神经科医生阿曼达·皮奎特 (Amanda Piquet) 说。

paras.en: For about a decade, Montgomery-Haga had lived with a debilitating autoimmune disease known as stiff person syndrome. The progressive condition can lock up the body’s muscles without warning, leading to falls, broken bones, excruciating pain and difficulty moving. Singer Celine Dion, who returned to the stage in September after years of battling the disease, has said it can feel “like somebody’s strangling you.”
paras.zh: 大约十年来，蒙哥马利-哈加一直患有一种使人衰弱的自身免疫性疾病，称为僵人综合症。这种进行性的病症会在没有警告的情况下锁住身体的肌肉，导致跌倒、骨折、剧痛和行动困难。歌手席琳·迪翁 (Celine Dion) 在与这种疾病作斗争多年后于 9 月重返舞台，她说感觉“就像有人勒死你一样”。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s own days were marked by dizziness, fatigue and pain. And sudden muscle spasms would send her sprawling. It was like the fainting goat videos popular on the internet, she says. “They get surprised and they fall over, and there’s nothing they can do about it.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加自己的日子充满了头晕、疲劳和疼痛。突然的肌肉痉挛会让她四肢瘫痪。她说，这就像互联网上流行的山羊晕倒视频。 “他们感到惊讶并摔倒，但他们对此无能为力。”

paras.en: But stiff person syndrome is no joke. It stripped Montgomery-Haga of her accounting job and her ability to drive. She couldn’t sit up in bed unless she had a safety bar to pull on. If she dropped the soap in the shower, it’d take her 10 minutes to pick it up.
paras.zh: 但僵人综合症可不是闹着玩的。这剥夺了蒙哥马利-哈加的会计工作和驾驶能力。除非有安全杆可以拉动，否则她无法在床上坐起来。如果她把肥皂掉在淋浴间里，她需要 10 分钟才能捡起来。

paras.en: Now, Montgomery-Haga hopes those struggles are finally coming to an end. That’s because a clinical trial with an experimental therapy has helped restore mobility for her — and others like her. She can stride through her living room again. She can landscape her front yard. She doesn’t have to brace herself when her dogs jump on her. And she hasn’t fallen once since the treatment. The change has been drastic, she says. “I’m just really excited about the future.”
paras.zh: 现在，蒙哥马利-哈加希望这些斗争最终能够结束。这是因为一项实验性疗法的临床试验帮助她和其他像她一样的人恢复了活动能力。她又可以大步穿过客厅了。她可以美化她的前院。当她的狗扑向她时，她不必支撑自己。自从接受治疗以来，她再也没有跌倒过一次。她说，变化是巨大的。 “我对未来感到非常兴奋。”

paras.en: The treatment, a type of CAR T cell therapy, extracts immune cells from a person’s body and engineers them to attack the very cells causing the disease. First used to fight cancer, CAR T is now also targeting a variety of autoimmune diseases. If given the green light by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Montgomery-Haga’s treatment would be the first such therapy approved for an autoimmune condition — and it would be the first approved treatment for stiff person syndrome.
paras.zh: 这种疗法是一种 CAR T 细胞疗法，从人体内提取免疫细胞，并改造它们来攻击引起疾病的细胞。 CAR T 最初用于对抗癌症，现在也用于治疗多种自身免疫性疾病。如果获得美国食品和药物管理局的批准，蒙哥马利-哈加的治疗将是第一个被批准用于自身免疫性疾病的治疗方法，并且这将是第一个被批准用于僵人综合症的治疗方法。

paras.en: Stiff person syndrome may be just the beginning, says Carl June, the University of Pennsylvania immunologist and oncologist who spearheaded CAR T cell therapy for cancer decades ago. The “living drug” could herald a new era of therapeutics for autoimmune diseases like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and even multiple sclerosis. “It’s revolutionary to think how far things have gone,” June says.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学免疫学家和肿瘤学家卡尔·琼 (Carl June) 表示，僵人综合症可能只是一个开始，几十年前他率先提出了 CAR T 细胞治疗癌症的方法。这种“活体药物”可能预示着狼疮、类风湿性关节炎甚至多发性硬化症等自身免疫性疾病治疗的新时代。 “想想事情已经走了多远，这是革命性的，”琼说。

paras.en: But he warns that it’s far too early to know if scientists have definitively cured stiff person syndrome. And there haven’t been enough people treated to get a good handle on all the possible side effects. “There could be long-term complications in autoimmune patients that don’t happen in our cancer patients,” he says. Other researchers urge caution. “It’s very important not to oversell it,” says Marc Scherlinger, a rheumatologist at Strasbourg University Hospital in France.
paras.zh: 但他警告说，现在判断科学家是否已经彻底治愈僵人综合症还为时过早。而且还没有足够多的人接受治疗来很好地处理所有可能的副作用。 “自身免疫患者可能会出现长期并发症，而我们的癌症患者不会发生这种情况，”他说。其他研究人员敦促谨慎行事。 “不要过度吹捧它，这一点非常重要，”法国斯特拉斯堡大学医院的风湿病学家马克·谢林格 (Marc Scherlinger) 说。

paras.en: For Piquet, one crucial question is how long the treatment will last. In Montgomery-Haga’s case, the answer seems to be at least two years. Montgomery-Haga still considers herself disabled, or “disabled-ish,” as she calls it. But when rating how she used to feel on a scale of one to 10, she’d put herself at a zero before treatment, she says. These days, she’s more like a seven.
paras.zh: 对于皮奎特来说，一个关键问题是治疗能持续多久。在蒙哥马利-哈加的例子中，答案似乎是至少两年。蒙哥马利-哈加仍然认为自己是残疾人，或者用她的话说，“有点残疾人”。但她说，当用 1 到 10 的等级来评估她过去的感受时，她在治疗前将自己的评分为零。如今，她更像是一个七岁的人了。

paras.en: What’s more, Montgomery-Haga says, “I think I’m still improving.”
paras.zh: 更重要的是，蒙哥马利-哈加说，“我认为我仍在进步。”

paras.en: There’s no single symptom that clued Montgomery-Haga in to her disease. In 2014, she started having difficulty picking things up off the floor. Then her boss asked her why she was limping — Montgomery-Haga hadn’t noticed. Her balance was off and her head felt weird, like “I was walking around in a fishbowl,” she says. It got to the point where Montgomery-Haga had difficulty crossing thresholds between rooms.
paras.zh: 没有任何单一症状表明蒙哥马利-哈加患有她的疾病。 2014年，她开始难以拾起地板上的东西。然后她的老板问她为什么一瘸一拐——蒙哥马利-哈加没有注意到。她失去了平衡，头感觉很奇怪，就像“我在鱼缸里走来走去”，她说。蒙哥马利-哈加已经很难跨过房间之间的门槛了。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga would startle easily, prompting her body to stiffen up like a board. One time when cooking, she burned her finger, spasmed and collapsed, cracking the back of her head on the cabinets. She lay on the floor crying, but finally managed to right herself. “As soon as you hit the floor,” she says, “your muscles are like, ‘Fine,’ and you can get up again.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加很容易受惊，身体就会像木板一样僵硬。有一次做饭时，她的手指被烫伤，痉挛并倒下，后脑勺撞到了柜子上。她躺在地板上哭泣，但最终还是站了起来。 “一旦你落地，”她说，“你的肌肉就会说，‘很好’，你就可以再次站起来了。”

paras.en: Those unpredictable symptoms capture a slice of what life is like with stiff person syndrome, or SPS. The disease, which affects roughly 2 in 100,000 people in the United States, typically develops in a person’s 30s or 40s. It is about twice as common in women as in men.
paras.zh: 这些不可预测的症状反映了僵人综合症（SPS）的生活情况。这种疾病在美国大约每 10 万人中就有 2 人受到影响，通常在 30 多岁或 40 多岁时发病。女性的发病率约为男性的两倍。

paras.en: Scientists don’t know what sets off the disease. But they think a person’s own antibodies start attacking a neurological network that helps muscles throughout the body relax. And when those tensed muscles are in opposition, like the biceps and triceps, they start fighting one another, Piquet says. That’s when people can end up in a stuck position, leading to stiffness. But because everyone’s immune system is different, patients’ experiences with the disease can vary greatly.
paras.zh: 科学家们不知道是什么引发了这种疾病。但他们认为，一个人自身的抗体开始攻击帮助全身肌肉放松的神经网络。皮奎特说，当这些紧张的肌肉（例如二头肌和三头肌）处于对立状态时，它们就会开始互相对抗。这时人们可能会陷入困境，导致僵硬。但由于每个人的免疫系统不同，患者的疾病经历可能会有很大差异。

paras.en: For Tara Zier, a former dentist based in Maryland, SPS started with extreme neck pain, blood pressure spikes, shortness of breath and feelings of impending doom. While some people struggle with mobility, Zier’s difficulties include standing and extreme fatigue. When she holds herself upright, her muscles clamp down on her spine like it’s in a vise. “Have you ever had a charley horse in your calf?” she asks. “Imagine one in your whole body that stops you in your tracks.”
paras.zh: 塔拉·齐尔 (Tara Zier) 是马里兰州的一名前牙医，SPS 开始时伴随着颈部极度疼痛、血压飙升、呼吸急促和厄运即将来临的感觉。虽然有些人行动不便，但齐尔的困难包括站立和极度疲劳。当她直立时，她的肌肉会像虎钳一样夹紧脊柱。 “你的小腿里曾经养过查理马吗？”她问。 “想象一下你全身有一个东西让你停下来。”

paras.en: Zier and Montgomery-Haga went years before learning what was behind their symptoms. Their cases mystified doctors — Zier saw 13 specialists and visited the emergency room nine times before getting a diagnosis. When she finally found out she had SPS three years after her first symptoms, Zier says she felt validated, like medicine was confirming what she already knew: “Something’s wrong with me.”
paras.zh: 齐尔和蒙哥马利-哈加花了很多年才了解他们症状背后的原因。他们的病例让医生感到困惑——齐尔在得到诊断之前看了 13 名专家并去了急诊室 9 次。齐尔说，当她在首次出现症状三年后终于发现自己患有 SPS 时，她感到自己得到了认可，就像医学证实了她已经知道的事情一样：“我有些问题。”

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s 2018 diagnosis put her “over the moon,” she says. For nearly four years, she had gotten sicker and sicker — but doctors couldn’t tell her why. She felt as if they were giving up on her. With the diagnosis, Montgomery-Haga not only learned that SPS existed, she says, “I was told it’s treatable.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加 2018 年的诊断让她“欣喜若狂”，她说。近四年来，她的病情越来越严重，但医生却无法告诉她原因。她觉得他们好像要放弃她了。通过诊断，蒙哥马利-哈加不仅了解到 SPS 的存在，她说，“我还被告知这是可以治疗的。”

paras.en: Current treatments include muscle relaxers, anti-seizure medications and Botox injections in body parts that feel especially stiff. Although these off-label therapies can address people’s symptoms, they’re “doing nothing to treat the underlying autoimmune disease,” Piquet says. And some can come with potent side effects, like mental fog.
paras.zh: 目前的治疗方法包括肌肉松弛剂、抗癫痫药物以及在感觉特别僵硬的身体部位注射肉毒杆菌。皮奎特说，尽管这些标签外疗法可以解决人们的症状，但它们“对治疗潜在的自身免疫性疾病没有任何作用”。有些可能会带来严重的副作用，比如精神迷雾。

paras.en: Zier, who has tried multiple combinations of different meds, remembers frequently losing her train of thought. She has since tapered off all but one drug, a low dose of Valium. “The trade-off,” she says, “is pain.”
paras.zh: 齐尔尝试过不同药物的多种组合，她记得经常失去思路。此后，她逐渐减少了除一种药物（低剂量的安定）外的所有药物的用量。 “代价是，”她说，“就是痛苦。”

paras.en: People with SPS can also receive intravenous infusions of healthy antibodies, a treatment called IVIG, to decrease muscle spasms and stiffness. Montgomery-Haga found it helpful but time-consuming. She’d go to the clinic every three weeks for an infusion, which could take up to six hours.
paras.zh: 患有 SPS 的人还可以接受静脉注射健康抗体（一种称为 IVIG 的治疗方法），以减少肌肉痉挛和僵硬。蒙哥马利-哈加发现这很有帮助，但很耗时。她每三周去一次诊所输液，这可能需要长达六个小时。

paras.en: “The bottom line is there are no FDA-approved therapies for this disease,” Piquet says. Now, the one most likely to cross the finish line first is something no one would have expected even a few years ago, CAR T pioneer June says. If you told doctors that CAR T cell therapy was going to be FDA approved for an autoimmune disease, he says, “people would have laughed.”
paras.zh: “最重要的是，目前还没有 FDA 批准的治疗这种疾病的疗法，”皮奎特说。 CAR T 先驱 June 表示，现在，最有可能第一个冲过终点线的人即使在几年前也没有人预料到。他说，如果你告诉医生 CAR T 细胞疗法将获得 FDA 批准用于治疗自身免疫性疾病，“人们会笑的。”

paras.en: June may be best known for his work in cancer, but he’s been keenly following the progress in auto-immune therapy. His daughter, now in her 30s, was diagnosed with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis when she was 9 years old. For her, that’s meant over 20 years of treatment with drugs that bring a bundle of side effects, such as fatigue and risk of infections. “It would be much better to be cured,” he says.
paras.zh: 琼最出名的可能是他在癌症方面的工作，但他一直在密切关注自身免疫治疗的进展。他的女儿现年30多岁，9岁时被诊断出患有幼年类风湿性关节炎。对她来说，这意味着 20 多年的药物治疗会带来一系列副作用，例如疲劳和感染风险。 “如果能被治愈就更好了，”他说。

paras.en: In autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and SPS, a person’s own antibodies attack tissues throughout the body, from blood vessels to cartilage to neurons. Wiping out these rogue antibodies can stop the attacks. But CAR T cell therapy doesn’t act on the antibodies themselves. It goes straight to the source, snuffing out the cellular factories that manufacture them.
paras.zh: 在类风湿性关节炎、狼疮和 SPS 等自身免疫性疾病中，人体自身的抗体会攻击全身的组织，从血管到软骨再到神经元。消灭这些流氓抗体可以阻止攻击。但 CAR T 细胞疗法并不作用于抗体本身。它直达源头，消灭制造它们的细胞工厂。

paras.en: Those antibody factories are known as B cells. To eliminate them, doctors recruit T cells, which act as the body’s security system and work together to hunt down and destroy problematic cells. In the lab, scientists fine-tune these hunters, outfitting them with a molecular homing device called a chimeric antigen receptor, or CAR. When infused back into patients’ bodies, the newly-engineered T cells can target the antibody factories directly — like a saboteur told exactly what to destroy.
paras.zh: 这些抗体工厂被称为 B 细胞。为了消除它们，医生招募 T 细胞，它们充当人体的安全系统，共同努力追捕并摧毁有问题的细胞。在实验室里，科学家们对这些猎人进行了微调，为它们配备了一种称为嵌合抗原受体（CAR）的分子归巢装置。当重新注入患者体内时，新设计的 T 细胞可以直接瞄准抗体工厂——就像破坏者确切地告诉要破坏什么一样。

paras.en: The CAR T cell therapy Lynn Montgomery-Haga received wipes out B cells, including the ones likely driving her disease. Doctors hope this therapy “resets” her immune system, getting rid of harmful B cells and letting healthy new ones take their place.
paras.zh: Lynn Montgomery-Haga 接受的 CAR T 细胞疗法消除了 B 细胞，包括可能导致她患病的细胞。医生希望这种疗法能够“重置”她的免疫系统，消除有害的 B 细胞，让健康的新细胞取而代之。

paras.en: “The secret behind CAR T cell therapy is that you completely deplete B cells in the body,” says Georg Schett, a rheumatologist at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg in Germany. Temporarily wiping out a person’s B cells lets the body replace them with fresh, unproblematic ones, Schett says. He calls it an “immune reset.”
paras.zh: “CAR T 细胞疗法背后的秘密是完全耗尽体内的 B 细胞，”德国埃尔兰根-纽伦堡弗里德里希-亚历山大大学的风湿病学家 Georg Schett 说。谢特说，暂时清除一个人的 B 细胞可以让身体用新鲜的、没有问题的 B 细胞取而代之。他称之为“免疫重置”。

paras.en: CAR T cell therapy got its start in the 2010s, when researchers used engineered T cells to target cancer. In 2017, the FDA approved the first CAR T cell therapies for two blood cancers, acute lymphoblastic leukemia and large B cell lymphoma. Soon after, scientists saw the first tantalizing hints that it might work for autoimmune diseases, too. In some cases, cancer patients with autoimmune disorders reported improvements in both conditions after treatment.
paras.zh: CAR T 细胞疗法始于 2010 年代，当时研究人员使用工程 T 细胞来靶向癌症。 2017年，FDA批准了首个CAR T细胞疗法用于治疗两种血癌：急性淋巴细胞白血病和大B细胞淋巴瘤。不久之后，科学家们看到了第一个诱人的迹象，表明它也可能对自身免疫性疾病有效。在某些情况下，患有自身免疫性疾病的癌症患者报告说，治疗后这两种情况都有所改善。

paras.en: But most researchers didn’t think it could be that easy, Schett says. After all, autoimmune diseases were driven by a complex network of cell types. How could targeting just one of them work?
paras.zh: 但大多数研究人员认为事情没那么容易，谢特说。毕竟，自身免疫性疾病是由复杂的细胞类型网络驱动的。只针对其中一个怎么可能有效呢？

paras.en: That thinking underwent a paradigm shift in 2021 when Schett and his team published the first major paper reporting a successful treatment with the therapy. The patient was a 20-year-old woman with a severe case of lupus, a complex, sometimes-fatal illness that can damage the kidneys and other organs. Within five weeks of CAR T cell therapy treatment, signs of her disease began to vanish.
paras.zh: 2021 年，当 Schett 和他的团队发表了第一篇报告该疗法成功治疗的重要论文时，这种想法发生了范式转变。患者是一名 20 岁女性，患有严重的狼疮，这是一种复杂的、有时甚至致命的疾病，会损害肾脏和其他器官。在接受 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗五周内，她的疾病迹象开始消失。

paras.en: Results like these were “unheard of,” says rheumatologist Maximilian Konig of Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore. Lupus is extremely difficult to treat, and for decades, most drugs tested against it failed. No one had ever seen the kind of improvements that Schett’s patient experienced.
paras.zh: 巴尔的摩约翰·霍普金斯医学院的风湿病学家马克西米利安·科尼格说，这样的结果“闻所未闻”。狼疮极难治疗，几十年来，大多数针对狼疮的药物测试都失败了。没有人见过谢特的病人所经历的那种改善。

paras.en: After the paper came out, “everybody was talking about it,” Konig says. Today, more than five years later, the woman’s lupus hasn’t returned, Schett says. “We consider this patient cured,” he says.
paras.zh: 论文发表后，“每个人都在谈论它，”科尼格说。谢特说，五年多后的今天，这位女士的狼疮还没有复发。 “我们认为这名患者已经治愈，”他说。

paras.en: The woman’s response was no fluke. The following year, Schett’s team reported similar results in five more lupus patients. All went into remission after CAR T cell therapy.
paras.zh: 女人的反应并非侥幸。第二年，谢特的团队在另外五名狼疮患者中报告了类似的结果。 CAR T 细胞治疗后，所有患者的病情均得到缓解。

paras.en: This was the true tipping point, June says. “It’s rare, very rare, that you get such striking results.”
paras.zh: 琼说，这是真正的转折点。 “能得到如此惊人的结果，非常罕见。”

paras.en: What followed was an explosion of research around the world. Scientists are now testing CAR T cell therapy in nearly a dozen autoimmune diseases linked to harmful B cells, including lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and a connective-tissue disease known as systemic sclerosis.
paras.zh: 随之而来的是世界各地研究的爆炸式增长。科学家们目前正在测试 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗近十几种与有害 B 细胞相关的自身免疫性疾病，包括狼疮、类风湿性关节炎和一种称为系统性硬化症的结缔组织疾病。

paras.en: Kyverna, the California-based company behind the SPS trial, is also running trials for neurological autoimmune conditions including generalized myasthenia gravis and progressive multiple sclerosis, or MS.
paras.zh: Kyverna 是一家总部位于加利福尼亚州的 SPS 试验背后的公司，该公司还在针对神经系统自身免疫性疾病进行试验，包括全身性重症肌无力和进行性多发性硬化症 (MS)。

paras.en: One reason using CAR T cell therapy for neurological conditions excites researchers is because of the cells’ potential to slip past the blood-brain barrier. That means they might be able to access pockets of smoldering inflammation inaccessible to other drugs, says neurologist Rebecca Farber of Columbia University.
paras.zh: 使用 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗神经系统疾病让研究人员兴奋的原因之一是这些细胞具有穿过血脑屏障的潜力。哥伦比亚大学神经学家丽贝卡·法伯说，这意味着它们可能能够接触到其他药物无法接触到的闷烧炎症区域。

paras.en: That could be a huge help in diseases like MS, in which a person’s antibodies attack the protective sheaths around nerve cells, causing numbness, brain fog and difficulty walking. Still, Farber doubts that CAR T cell therapy could fix existing damage. “We’re not expecting it to repair the nervous system,” she says. But it’s possible the treatment could freeze the disease’s progress. Patients are already asking her team about future treatments.
paras.zh: 这可能对治疗多发性硬化症等疾病有很大帮助，在这种疾病中，人的抗体会攻击神经细胞周围的保护鞘，导致麻木、脑雾和行走困难。尽管如此，法伯仍怀疑 CAR T 细胞疗法能否修复现有损伤。 “我们并不指望它能修复神经系统，”她说。但这种治疗有可能阻止疾病的进展。患者已经向她的团队询问未来的治疗方法。

paras.en: For Piquet, who cares for roughly 100 people with SPS, Kyverna’s trial offered a compelling opportunity to help her patients. Montgomery-Haga cried when Piquet told her about the trial at one of their regular Zoom appointments. She recalls wondering, is this the treatment that “might help me be normal again?”
paras.zh: 对于负责照顾大约 100 名 SPS 患者的 Piquet 来说，Kyverna 的试验为帮助她的患者提供了一个令人信服的机会。当皮奎特在他们定期的 Zoom 约会中告诉蒙哥马利-哈加有关审判时，蒙哥马利-哈加哭了。她回忆道，她当时想，这种治疗“可能会帮助我恢复正常吗？”

paras.en: The good, the bad and the potentially ugly
paras.zh: 好的、坏的和潜在的丑陋

paras.en: Though Montgomery-Haga leapt at the chance to try Kyverna’s treatment, called miv-cel, CAR T cell therapy is no walk in the park. Before starting, doctors sit patients down to “talk about the good, the bad and the potentially ugly,” Piquet says.
paras.zh: 尽管 Montgomery-Haga 抓住了机会尝试 Kyverna 的治疗方法 miv-cel，但 CAR T 细胞疗法并不是在公园里散步。皮奎特说，在开始之前，医生会让病人坐下来“谈论好的、坏的和可能丑陋的事情”。

paras.en: That includes the rigorous prep work needed before people receive their engineered T cells. Patients must first get low-dose chemotherapy, which flushes T cells from the body and makes space for the new ones. Chemo can ambush the body with symptoms including hair thinning, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
paras.zh: 这包括人们接受工程 T 细胞之前所需的严格准备工作。患者必须首先接受低剂量化疗，将 T 细胞从体内清除，并为新细胞腾出空间。化疗可能会给身体带来一些症状，包括头发稀疏、恶心、呕吐和腹泻。

paras.en: Treatment itself also carries risks. It destroys most B cells in the body — not just the ones that cause disease. That can lead to fever, inflammation and potentially risky infections. In Kyverna’s trial, for example, 15 percent of participants had severely low white blood cell counts after treatment. Such symptoms were expected, Piquet says, and were easily treated.
paras.zh: 治疗本身也存在风险。它会破坏体内的大多数 B 细胞，而不仅仅是导致疾病的 B 细胞。这可能会导致发烧、炎症和潜在的危险感染。例如，在 Kyverna 的试验中，15% 的参与者在治疗后白细胞计数严重偏低。皮奎特说，这种症状是预料之中的，而且很容易治疗。

paras.en: Other CAR T treatments seem to have fared far worse. In August, the pharmaceutical company Novartis paused clinical trials of its therapy, rap-cel, across a spectrum of autoimmune diseases after three patients died. Bristol Myers Squibb has also paused similar studies after some patients experienced neurological complications, according to the Wall Street Journal. Details of the incidents were slow to emerge and have set the field on edge. “It’s a tragedy,” Konig says. He calls such outcomes an important wake-up call.
paras.zh: Other CAR T treatments seem to have fared far worse.八月，诺华制药公司在三名患者死亡后暂停了其治疗多种自身免疫性疾病的疗法 rap-cel 的临床试验。据《华尔街日报》报道，在一些患者出现神经系统并发症后，百时美施贵宝也暂停了类似的研究。 Details of the incidents were slow to emerge and have set the field on edge. “这是一场悲剧，”科尼格说。 He calls such outcomes an important wake-up call.

paras.en: But red flags in one trial don’t mean all CAR T products are dangerous, Konig says. That’s because many different designs and manufacturing processes exist, and scientists can’t always predict what will make one product toxic and another safe. Kyverna’s miv-cel, for instance, has been consistently well-tolerated in the more than 100 patients treated, a spokesperson for the company says.
paras.zh: 但科尼格说，一项试验中的危险信号并不意味着所有 CAR T 产品都是危险的。这是因为存在许多不同的设计和制造工艺，科学家无法总能预测什么会使一种产品有毒而另一种产品安全。例如，该公司发言人表示，Kyverna 的 miv-cel 在 100 多名接受治疗的患者中一直表现出良好的耐受性。

paras.en: CAR T cell therapies are transformative, Konig says. “They’re going to change the field — but there are risks.”
paras.zh: Konig 说，CAR T 细胞疗法具有变革性。 “他们将改变这个领域——但也存在风险。”

paras.en: Another risk is that the once-vanquished disease will return. Doctors don’t know all the genetic and environmental conditions that trigger autoimmune disease. Some researchers wonder whether vulnerable individuals remain vulnerable, even after treatment. But because it often takes multiple insults for someone to tip into a state of disease, Scherlinger says, CAR T cell therapy could buy patients lots of time.
paras.zh: 另一个风险是曾经被战胜的疾病将会卷土重来。医生并不了解引发自身免疫性疾病的所有遗传和环境条件。一些研究人员想知道，即使在接受治疗后，脆弱的个体是否仍然脆弱。但谢林格表示，由于一个人往往需要多次受到伤害才会陷入疾病状态，因此 CAR T 细胞疗法可以为患者赢得大量时间。

paras.en: After 10 days in the hospital for her treatment, Montgomery-Haga returned to recover at home. In the following months, she started to notice some changes. It was easier getting around the house, for one. And she felt her balance and stability improving. She can now kneel down to garden and clean without the days of recovery it used to require. “I can vacuum my house,” she says. “It seems so little, but now I can vacuum!”
paras.zh: After 10 days in the hospital for her treatment, Montgomery-Haga returned to recover at home. In the following months, she started to notice some changes.一方面，在房子里走动更容易。 And she felt her balance and stability improving. She can now kneel down to garden and clean without the days of recovery it used to require. “我可以给我的房子吸尘，”她说。 “看起来很小，但现在我可以吸尘了！”

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga can even sit down “crisscross applesauce,” she says. “I couldn’t do that for, like, 10 years.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加甚至可以坐下来“纵横交错的苹果酱”，她说。 “我大概有 10 年都做不到这一点。”

paras.en: Four months after the treatment, Piquet’s team tested Montgomery-Haga’s walking ability. In a hallway at University of Colorado Anschutz’s research building, the team marked out 25 feet with little orange cones. At one end stood Montgomery-Haga. At the other, Piquet watched behind a video camera. This time, Montgomery-Haga’s gait was smooth and her arms were down, not hovering out into the air to catch herself if she fell. “You could see that she was walking with a lot more confidence,” Piquet says.
paras.zh: 治疗四个月后，皮奎特的团队测试了蒙哥马利-哈加的步行能力。在科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校研究大楼的走廊里，研究小组用橙色小锥体标记了 25 英尺。蒙哥马利-哈加站在一端。另一方面，皮奎特在摄像机后面观看。这一次，蒙哥马利-哈加的步态平稳，双臂垂下，不会在摔倒时悬停在空中接住自己。 “你可以看到她走路时更加自信了，”皮奎特说。

paras.en: The team saw similar results in other SPS patients. Some who had difficulty walking before treatment now wanted to run, Piquet says. “It’s incredible to just see those patients speeding down the hallway.” She remembers smiles, high fives and a sense of celebration in the air. Eight of 12 people who had used a walking aid for the initial test didn’t need one for the follow-up, Piquet reported at the American Academy of Neurology meeting in April.
paras.zh: 研究小组在其他 SPS 患者中也看到了类似的结果。皮奎特说，一些在治疗前行走困难的人现在想跑步。 “看到那些病人在走廊上疾驰，真是令人难以置信。”她记得微笑、击掌和空气中的庆祝气氛。皮奎特在 4 月份的美国神经病学学会会议上报告说，在初次测试中使用助行器的 12 人中有 8 人在后续测试中不需要助行器。

paras.en: In September, Kyverna reported the trial’s one-year results: Patients maintained mobility improvements, with a third completing their 25-foot walk about as fast as a healthy adult. Additionally, nearly all patients no longer rely on immuno-suppressive drugs to tamp down harmful immune activity. That’s good news because such drugs can bring all sorts of nasty side effects, like vomiting, bleeding and infections.
paras.zh: 9 月，Kyverna 报告了该试验的一年结果：患者的活动能力保持改善，三分之一的患者完成 25 英尺步行的速度与健康成年人的速度相当。此外，几乎所有患者都不再依赖免疫抑制药物来抑制有害的免疫活动。这是个好消息，因为此类药物会带来各种令人讨厌的副作用，如呕吐、出血和感染。

paras.en: The results with SPS are “really something to celebrate,” June says. But only time and many more treatments will reveal how safe CAR T really is, he says.
paras.zh: June 说，SPS 的成果“确实值得庆祝”。但他说，只有时间和更多的治疗才能揭示 CAR T 的真正安全性。

paras.en: That’s a concern for Zier, who says she wouldn’t feel comfortable trying the therapy at this point. Zier doesn’t know how she’d respond. She’s a single mother with two kids; even a rare side effect could disrupt her life in a way she may not be able to manage. And these days, she’s managing as well as she can. Zier is the founder and CEO of The Stiff Person Syndrome Research Foundation, which supports research for SPS treatments.
paras.zh: 这是齐尔担心的问题，她说她现在不愿意尝试这种疗法。紫儿不知道自己会作何反应。她是一位有两个孩子的单亲妈妈；即使是罕见的副作用也可能以她无法应对的方式扰乱她的生活。如今，她已经尽力做到最好了。 Zier 是僵人综合症研究基金会的创始人兼首席执行官，该基金会支持 SPS 治疗研究。

paras.en: Kyverna is in the process of submitting miv-cel for FDA approval. The company is seeking priority review and hopes the treatment might be available to patients in 2027. If SPS is the first autoimmune disease to have an FDA-approved CAR T cell therapy, myasthenia gravis could be the second, says Warner Biddle, Kyverna’s CEO. What’s more, miv-cel also appeared to improve symptoms in six patients with severe cases of rheumatoid arthritis, researchers reported in August in Nature Medicine.
paras.zh: Kyverna 正在向 FDA 提交 miv-cel 的批准。该公司正在寻求优先审查，并希望在 2027 年为患者提供该治疗方法。Kyverna 首席执行官 Warner Biddle 表示，如果 SPS 是第一个获得 FDA 批准的 CAR T 细胞疗法的自身免疫性疾病，那么重症肌无力可能是第二个。此外，研究人员在 8 月的《自然医学》杂志上报道称，miv-cel 似乎还改善了 6 名严重类风湿关节炎患者的症状。

paras.en: As for what’s next, the door is wide open. Some scientists are working to make off-the-shelf forms of CAR T that wouldn’t require personalized engineering. Others are trying to reprogram T cells directly inside people’s bodies, rather than in the lab. Still others are trying to make T cells that target only the B cells responsible for disease. In the future, doctors might use such drugs to help patients avoid the cumbersome treatment process that Montgomery-Haga endured.
paras.zh: 至于接下来的事情，大门是敞开的。一些科学家正在致力于制造不需要个性化工程的现成 CAR T 形式。其他人则试图直接在人体内而不是在实验室中对 T 细胞进行重新编程。还有一些人正在尝试制造只针对导致疾病的 B 细胞的 T 细胞。未来，医生可能会使用此类药物来帮助患者避免蒙哥马利-哈加所经历的繁琐治疗过程。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s own future looks far different than what she had imagined a few years ago. In 2026, she took a trip to Washington, D.C., to see the monuments. Now she’d like to visit Paris, Scotland and Ireland, too.
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加自己的未来看起来与她几年前的想象大不相同。 2026年，她前往华盛顿特区参观了这些纪念碑。现在她也想去巴黎、苏格兰和爱尔兰。

paras.en: For so many years, Montgomery-Haga has looked at trips and activities — and even household chores — that most people take for granted, thinking, “Man, I wish I could do that,” she says. “Now I can.”
paras.zh: 多年来，蒙哥马利-哈加一直关注大多数人认为理所当然的旅行和活动，甚至家务，她说：“伙计，我希望我能做到这一点。” “现在我可以了。”

articles.title: Physicists May Have Inadvertently Built a Qubit That Can Run Backward in Time
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: In the classical Universe, the arrow of time flies one way – but in the quantum realm, where classical physics breaks down, could even time's direction be ripe for the tweaking?
paras.zh: 在经典宇宙中，时间之箭是单向飞行的——但在经典物理学崩溃的量子领域，时间的方向是否已经成熟，可以进行调整了？

paras.en: The ability to manipulate the direction of quantum evolution could offer new ways to process information – with implications especially for quantum computing.
paras.zh: 操纵量子演化方向的能力可以提供处理信息的新方法——尤其对量子计算具有影响。

paras.en: Korean physicists have demonstrated a qubit whose processes can be run backward in time… and the deliciously ironic twist is that they had to go back in time to find it.
paras.zh: 韩国物理学家已经展示了一种量子位，其过程可以向后运行……而讽刺的是，他们必须回到过去才能找到它。

paras.en: In a new preprint, physicist Tai Hyun Yoon of Korea University developed a theory describing what he calls a quantum vacuum-seeded single-photon time qubit – and showed that an experiment he and colleagues conducted in 2018 for an entirely different purpose had inadvertently already shown it in action.
paras.zh: 在一份新的预印本中，高丽大学的物理学家 Tai Hyun Yoon 提出了一种理论，描述了他所谓的量子真空种子单光子时间量子位，并表明他和同事在 2018 年为完全不同的目的进行的一项实验已经无意中展示了它的实际效果。

paras.en: The notion of a time qubit is a relatively recent one, arising in a preprint penned by physicist Yakov Bloch of Tel Aviv University, uploaded to arXiv in November 2025.
paras.zh: 时间量子位的概念是一个相对较新的概念，出现在特拉维夫大学物理学家 Yakov Bloch 撰写的预印本中，并于 2025 年 11 月上传到 arXiv。

paras.en: It's not actually a qubit that can travel backward in time; rather, as Bloch explains it, it's a quantum system that can evolve in two opposite temporal directions at once.
paras.zh: 它实际上并不是一个可以时光倒流的量子位；它只是一个量子比特。相反，正如布洛赫所解释的那样，它是一个可以同时沿两个相反的时间方向演化的量子系统。

paras.en: Imagine a clock whose hands can run both clockwise and counterclockwise simultaneously. That's roughly the idea – except that instead of turning back time itself, the qubit allows physicists to manipulate the direction in which a quantum process unfolds.
paras.zh: 想象一个时钟，它的指针可以同时顺时针和逆时针运行。大致的想法就是这样——只不过量子位不是让时间本身倒转，而是让物理学家能够操纵量子过程展开的方向。

paras.en: He proposed that this could be experimentally tested by splitting the path of a quantum particle in two, with opposing magnetic fields along the two paths, then bringing them back together. The interference pattern of their reunion could reveal how the two opposing evolutions are connected.
paras.zh: 他提出，可以通过将量子粒子的路径一分为二，沿着两条路径施加相反的磁场，然后将它们重新组合在一起来进行实验测试。他们重聚的干涉模式可以揭示这两种相反的进化是如何联系在一起的。

paras.en: As of time of writing, that idea remains solidly in the theoretical realm; but, like a quantum particle split in two, Yoon took the idea and ran with it in another direction.
paras.zh: 截至撰写本文时，这一想法仍然牢牢停留在理论领域。但是，就像量子粒子一分为二一样，尹接受了这个想法，并将其带向另一个方向。

paras.en: Instead of using magnetic fields to reverse the evolution of a spinning particle, Yoon turned to light. His approach uses two crystal sources that generate entangled photon pairs; one photon from each pair carries the single-photon qubit. The technique is called entangled nonlinear biphoton source (ENBS) interferometry.
paras.zh: 尹没有使用磁场来逆转旋转粒子的演化，而是转向了光。他的方法使用两个产生纠缠光子对的晶体源；每对中的一个光子携带单光子量子位。该技术称为纠缠非线性双光子源（ENBS）干涉测量。

paras.en: The direction of a particular quantum interaction is then controlled by adjusting the phase of the light used to generate the photons.
paras.zh: 然后通过调整用于产生光子的光的相位来控制特定量子相互作用的方向。

paras.en: Tweaking the phase by half a cycle reverses the quantum interaction – not because time itself is flowing backward, but because the mathematical process governing the interaction runs in the opposite direction.
paras.zh: 将相位调整半个周期会反转量子相互作用——不是因为时间本身在倒流，而是因为控制相互作用的数学过程朝相反的方向运行。

paras.en: In quantum mechanics, the evolution of a system over time is governed by a mathematical description called a Hamiltonian. It determines how the system's quantum state changes from one moment to the next.
paras.zh: 在量子力学中，系统随时间的演化受到称为哈密顿量的数学描述的控制。它决定了系统的量子态从一个时刻到下一个时刻如何变化。

paras.en: Reverse the sign of that Hamiltonian, and the system evolves as though time itself were running backward, retracing the changes it would otherwise undergo.
paras.zh: 反转哈密顿量的符号，系统就会不断演化，就好像时间本身在倒退一样，追溯它本来会经历的变化。

paras.en: Yoon's method doesn't reverse the entire Hamiltonian, but it does reverse the part governing the interaction he controls. This gives him two opposing directions of quantum evolution – the equivalent of a quantum clock whose hands can turn either way.
paras.zh: Yoon 的方法并没有反转整个哈密顿量，但确实反转了他控制的相互作用的部分。这给了他两个相反的量子进化方向——相当于一个指针可以向任意方向转动的量子钟。

paras.en: But two opposing directions are not in themselves a time qubit. That requires something extra – superposition, where both directions exist simultaneously.
paras.zh: 但两个相反的方向本身并不是时间量子位。这需要一些额外的东西——叠加，两个方向同时存在。

paras.en: This is where the shared laser light becomes important. Ordinarily, generating a photon pair leaves behind information that could reveal which crystal produced it. That information distinguishes the two possible paths, preventing them from producing the coherent superposition needed for a qubit.
paras.zh: 这就是共享激光变得重要的地方。通常，产生光子对会留下可以揭示是哪个晶体产生它的信息。该信息区分了两种可能的路径，防止它们产生量子位所需的相干叠加。

paras.en: But by supplying both crystals with light from the same coherent laser source, the distinguishing information can be suppressed, allowing the two opposing quantum evolutions to interfere.
paras.zh: 但是，通过向两个晶体提供来自同一相干激光源的光，可以抑制区别信息，从而允许两种相反的量子演化发生干涉。

paras.en: The result is a single-photon qubit that encodes not just two different paths, but two opposing directions of quantum evolution.
paras.zh: 结果是一个单光子量子位不仅编码两条不同的路径，而且编码两个相反的量子演化方向。

paras.en: Yoon didn't need to design and build an entirely new experiment to show this approach is feasible. Instead, he turned to measurements from experiments he and colleagues had already conducted, including one in 2018.
paras.zh: Yoon 不需要设计和构建一个全新的实验来证明这种方法是可行的。相反，他转向了他和同事已经进行的实验（包括 2018 年的一项实验）的测量结果。

paras.en: Those experiments had demonstrated the phase-dependent behavior and interference that his new theoretical framework requires. By reexamining the data he and his colleagues had already collected, Yoon showed that the apparatus could be understood as an implementation of a single-photon time qubit.
paras.zh: 这些实验证明了他的新理论框架所需的相位相关行为和干扰。通过重新检查他和同事已经收集的数据，尹表明该设备可以被理解为单光子时间量子位的实现。

paras.en: Because it uses data from older experiments to probe a new theory, it's not a perfect demonstration. However, as a proof of concept, it suggests there could be a lot to gain by pursuing it in a dedicated investigation of time qubits.
paras.zh: 因为它使用旧实验的数据来探索新理论，所以它并不是一个完美的演示。然而，作为概念证明，它表明通过对时间量子位的专门研究来追求它可能会获得很多收获。

paras.en: A more specialized experiment with tighter control over the quantum states could test the full range of operations predicted by the theory.
paras.zh: 对量子态进行更严格控制的更专业的实验可以测试该理论预测的全部操作。

paras.en: Or, as Yoon puts it, "Coupling the discrete ENBS time qubit via controlled time-frequency displacements to hardware-native Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TF-GKP) bosonic grid states in chronocyclic phase space establishes a robust pathway toward fault-tolerant temporal quantum error correction, high-dimensional qudit processing, and tabletop simulations of relativistic quantum detector dynamics."
paras.zh: 或者，正如 Yoon 所说，“通过受控时频位移将离散 ENBS 时间量子位与时间循环相空间中的硬件原生 Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TF-GKP) 玻色网格状态耦合，建立了一条通往容错时间量子纠错、高维量子处理和相对论量子探测器动力学桌面模拟的稳健途径。”

paras.en: The research, which has yet to be peer-reviewed, is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究尚未经过同行评审，可在 arXiv 上获取。

articles.title: Scientists May Have Discovered Why Men's Prostates Enlarge With Age
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Scientists have discovered a distinct subtype of cell in the prostate, and it could help solve the mystery of why the gland enlarges with age.
paras.zh: 科学家们在前列腺中发现了一种独特的细胞亚型，它可能有助于解开前列腺为何随着年龄增长而增大的谜团。

paras.en: This natural phenomenon is called benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and it tends to occur in just one region of the prostate.
paras.zh: 这种自然现象称为良性前列腺增生 (BPH)，它往往只发生在前列腺的一个区域。

paras.en: But scientists still don't understand why.
paras.zh: 但科学家们仍然不明白为什么。

paras.en: Now, researchers at Johns Hopkins University have found a possible culprit hiding around the urethra.
paras.zh: 现在，约翰·霍普金斯大学的研究人员发现了可能的罪魁祸首隐藏在尿道周围。

paras.en: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, the team has identified a population of prostate cells that are particularly abundant in this region, especially in cases of BPH.
paras.zh: 通过单细胞 RNA 测序，研究小组确定了该区域特别丰富的前列腺细胞群，尤其是在 BPH 病例中。

paras.en: The findings are published in The Journal of Pathology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《病理学杂志》上。

paras.en: "Although BPH affects millions of men worldwide, scientists still do not fully understand why it develops primarily in a region of the prostate known as the transition zone, while other regions of the gland remain relatively unaffected," explains senior author Vasan Yegnasubramanian.
paras.zh: 资深作者 Vasan Yegnasubramanian 解释说：“尽管前列腺增生症影响着全世界数百万男性，但科学家们仍然不完全明白为什么它主要发生在前列腺的一个称为过渡区的区域，而腺体的其他区域相对不受影响。”

paras.en: The transition zone is the part of the prostate that surrounds the urethra.
paras.zh: 过渡区是前列腺周围尿道的部分。

paras.en: If this area enlarges with age, it can constrict the passage, making urination slower and more sporadic.
paras.zh: 如果这个区域随着年龄的增长而扩大，它会收缩通道，使排尿更慢、更不规律。

paras.en: It's the most common prostate problem in men older than age 50, and while changes to hormone levels, inflammation, and cellular growth probably play a role, no one really knows why, at a cellular level, BPH occurs.
paras.zh: 这是 50 岁以上男性最常见的前列腺问题，虽然激素水平、炎症和细胞生长的变化可能发挥了一定作用，但没有人真正知道为什么在细胞水平上会发生 BPH。

paras.en: Urologist Charles Welliver at Albany Medical College was not involved in the recent study, but in an interview for the Urology Care Foundation's podcast in August, he explained that BPH isn't due to swelling.
paras.zh: 奥尔巴尼医学院的泌尿科医生 Charles Welliver 没有参与最近的研究，但在 8 月份接受泌尿科护理基金会播客采访时，他解释说 BPH 并不是由肿胀引起的。

paras.en: "Benign prostatic hyperplasia is just an increase in the number of cells within the prostate," said Welliver.
paras.zh: “良性前列腺增生只是前列腺内细胞数量的增加，”韦利弗说。

paras.en: "So, the cells don't get bigger, there's an increase in the number."
paras.zh: “所以，细胞并没有变大，而是数量增加了。”

paras.en: Now, scientists think they have figured out which units might be behind that cellular surge.
paras.zh: 现在，科学家们认为他们已经弄清楚哪些单位可能是细胞激增的幕后黑手。

paras.en: Researchers at Johns Hopkins analyzed noncancerous prostate tissue from 10 men who had prostate cancer.
paras.zh: 约翰·霍普金斯大学的研究人员分析了 10 名患有前列腺癌的男性的非癌性前列腺组织。

paras.en: Samples came from the three major zones of the prostate, and researchers carefully analyzed which genes were turned on or off in nearly 130,000 individual cells.
paras.zh: 样本来自前列腺的三个主要区域，研究人员仔细分析了近 130,000 个单个细胞中哪些基因被打开或关闭。

paras.en: In tissues from the transition zone and in samples from BPH, researchers found a distinct cell population that was rare in other parts of the prostate.
paras.zh: 在移行区组织和前列腺增生症样本中，研究人员发现了前列腺其他部位罕见的独特细胞群。

paras.en: These cells are a subtype of basal cells called WIF1+, and they are transcriptionally and anatomically distinct to the rest of their family members.
paras.zh: 这些细胞是称为 WIF1+ 的基底细胞亚型，它们在转录和解剖学上与其家族其他成员不同。

paras.en: Scientists say they display a unique gene expression profile, and RNA sequencing and staining show that they are markedly enriched in the transition zone of the human prostate.
paras.zh: 科学家表示，它们表现出独特的基因表达谱，RNA测序和染色表明它们在人类前列腺的过渡区显着富集。

paras.en: Some genes associated with WIF1+ cells respond to androgens like testosterone and are involved in signaling pathways that influence prostate growth and development.
paras.zh: 一些与 WIF1+ 细胞相关的基因会对睾酮等雄激素做出反应，并参与影响前列腺生长和发育的信号通路。

paras.en: "Together," the authors write, "the molecular signature, zonal distribution, and pathway enrichment suggest that transition-zone-enriched WIF1+ basal cells may contribute to BPH pathogenesis by promoting epithelial and stromal remodeling."
paras.zh: 作者写道，“总而言之，分子特征、区域分布和通路富集表明，过渡区富集的 WIF1+ 基底细胞可能通过促进上皮和基质重塑而促进 BPH 发病机制。”

paras.en: The researchers also speculate that by dampening inflammation and a growth-signaling pathway called WNT, these cells could help explain why prostate cancer starts less often in the transition zone.
paras.zh: 研究人员还推测，通过抑制炎症和名为 WNT 的生长信号通路，这些细胞可以帮助解释为什么前列腺癌在移行区较少发生。

paras.en: "The analysis revealed that these cells possess molecular features associated with tissue remodeling that could contribute to prostate enlargement as well as an ability to communicate with neighboring cells, suggesting they may help establish the unique biological environment of the transition zone," says first author Rulin Wang.
paras.zh: 第一作者王儒林说：“分析表明，这些细胞具有与组织重塑相关的分子特征，可能有助于前列腺增大，并且具有与邻近细胞沟通的能力，这表明它们可能有助于建立过渡区独特的生物环境。”

paras.en: When Wang and colleagues analyzed publicly available datasets, they found more evidence to support their results.
paras.zh: 当王和同事分析公开数据集时，他们发现了更多证据来支持他们的结果。

paras.en: Enlarged prostate gland tissues were enriched with WIF1+ basal cells.
paras.zh: 增大的前列腺组织富含 WIF1+ 基底细胞。

paras.en: The gene signature of these abundant basal cells was also distinctly altered.
paras.zh: 这些丰富的基底细胞的基因特征也明显改变。

paras.en: Wang says this raises the possibility that these cells "contribute to the regional processes that make the transition zone particularly susceptible to BPH."
paras.zh: 王说，这提出了一种可能性，即这些细胞“有助于使过渡区特别容易受到前列腺增生症影响的区域过程”。

paras.en: For now, that's just a hypothesis, but it's one that Wang and colleagues think deserves further investigation.
paras.zh: 目前，这只是一个假设，但王和同事认为值得进一步研究。

paras.en: Future studies, for instance, could examine the functional roles of WIF1+ basal cells in the development of enlarged prostate glands.
paras.zh: 例如，未来的研究可以检查 WIF1+ 基底细胞在增大的前列腺发育中的功能作用。

paras.en: If these cells really do play a direct role in BPH, they could become future drug targets.
paras.zh: 如果这些细胞确实在良性前列腺增生中发挥直接作用，它们可能成为未来的药物靶点。

paras.en: The research has been published in The Journal of Pathology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《病理学杂志》上。

articles.title: Uranium Waste From This Aussie Mine Was Safely Locked Away, But Microbes Had Other Plans
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: In 1944, rocks from the Mount Painter mine in the heart of Australia were sent to the US for experiments as part of the Manhattan Project.
paras.zh: 1944 年，作为曼哈顿计划的一部分，澳大利亚中部佩因特山矿的岩石被送往美国进行实验。

paras.en: The repercussions of those actions left deep scars across the world.
paras.zh: 这些行动的影响给世界各地留下了深深的伤痕。

paras.en: At Mount Painter, though, scientists believed the mine's uranium and rare earth elements were more or less safely locked away in the dry waste piles (a.k.a. tailings).
paras.zh: 然而，在佩因特山，科学家们相信该矿的铀和稀土元素或多或少被安全地锁在干燥废物堆（又称尾矿）中。

paras.en: The site was eventually closed in 1965 and later incorporated into Arkaroola Wilderness Sanctuary.
paras.zh: 该遗址最终于 1965 年关闭，后来并入阿卡鲁拉荒野保护区。

paras.en: But recent samples taken from the surface of tailings at Mount Painter's Number 6 Workings suggest the site may not be as safe as we thought.
paras.zh: 但最近从佩因特山 6 号矿场尾矿表面采集的样本表明，该地点可能并不像我们想象的那么安全。

paras.en: These tailings have supposedly lain undisturbed for more than 80 years.
paras.zh: 据推测，这些尾矿已经静静地放置了 80 多年。

paras.en: But something has been moving potentially dangerous minerals to the surface of the waste piles, where they have accumulated at unexpectedly high concentrations.
paras.zh: 但有某种东西正在将潜在危险的矿物质转移到废物堆的表面，并在那里以意想不到的高浓度积累。

paras.en: In a study recently published in the Journal of Hazardous Materials, researchers suggest that microbes in the rubble are transporting these toxic substances to the top 10cm of the waste, in the form of polymetallic nanoparticles.
paras.zh: 在最近发表在《危险材料杂志》上的一项研究中，研究人员认为，瓦砾中的微生物正在将这些有毒物质以多金属纳米颗粒的形式输送到废物顶部 10 厘米处。

paras.en: "We have traditionally assumed that these toxic metals were securely locked away by nature in these arid environments, but these tiny organisms are proving us wrong," says geoscientist Joël Brugger.
paras.zh: “我们传统上认为这些有毒金属被大自然安全地锁定在这些干旱的环境中，但这些微小的生物体证明我们错了，”地球科学家乔尔·布鲁格说。

paras.en: "They are essentially acting as microscopic factories, breaking down stable minerals and mobilizing elements like uranium into the surrounding ecosystem."
paras.zh: “它们本质上就像微型工厂，分解稳定的矿物质，并将铀等元素转移到周围的生态系统中。”

paras.en: Further studies will be needed to confirm that the microbes are actually responsible for the changes seen in these tailings.
paras.zh: 需要进一步的研究来确认微生物实际上是造成这些尾矿中所见变化的原因。

paras.en: But for now, it's the scientists' best guess, as there aren't many other good explanations.
paras.zh: 但就目前而言，这是科学家们的最佳猜测，因为没有太多其他好的解释。

paras.en: In other parts of the world, researchers have also documented radiation-resistant microbes interacting with uranium waste.
paras.zh: 在世界其他地区，研究人员还记录了抗辐射微生物与铀废物的相互作用。

paras.en: The biggest concern is that these microbes appear to be converting the minerals from insoluble phosphates into colloidal forms that can easily travel through the environment.
paras.zh: 最令人担忧的是，这些微生物似乎正在将矿物质从不溶性磷酸盐转化为可以轻松在环境中传播的胶体形式。

paras.en: Rain is rare in semi-arid Arkaroola, arriving in the form of sudden summer thunderstorms. Converted into colloids, minerals like uranium are readily suspended in rainwater, which could carry them much further from the mine site, especially during the flash flooding that sometimes occurs in Arkaroola.
paras.zh: 半干旱的阿卡鲁拉很少下雨，以夏季突然的雷暴雨的形式到来。铀等矿物质转化为胶体后，很容易悬浮在雨水中，这可能会将它们带到距离矿区更远的地方，特别是在阿卡鲁拉有时发生山洪期间。

paras.en: Toxic and radioactive minerals like uranium and rare earth elements are not what you want sprinkled throughout the soil and waterways.
paras.zh: 您不希望将铀和稀土元素等有毒和放射性矿物质撒在土壤和水道中。

paras.en: Uranium is highly radioactive, and exposure to it – for instance, by drinking contaminated water or inhaling tiny particles – can cause serious damage to humans and other living things.
paras.zh: 铀具有高放射性，接触它（例如通过饮用受污染的水或吸入微小颗粒）可能会对人类和其他生物造成严重损害。

paras.en: The paper calls for a serious rethink of how we deal with mining waste.
paras.zh: 该文件呼吁认真重新思考我们如何处理采矿废物。

paras.en: While Arkaroola is protected from further mining, its radioactive legacy is clearly not over yet.
paras.zh: 虽然阿卡鲁拉受到保护，免遭进一步开采，但其放射性遗产显然尚未结束。

paras.en: Mount Painter's Number 6 Workings is just one of many mines left abandoned after the proliferation of nuclear weapons during the 20th century.
paras.zh: 佩因特山 6 号矿井只是 20 世纪核武器扩散后被遗弃的众多矿井之一。

paras.en: But uranium production continues across the world. And there's never been such a great demand for metals and minerals.
paras.zh: 但世界各地的铀生产仍在继续。对金属和矿物的需求从未如此之大。

paras.en: "As a result of continuing global development, the transformation of the world's energy infrastructure away from fossil fuels, and the electrification of transport infrastructure, demand for base metals such as copper, critical minerals such as rare earth elements, and energy minerals such as uranium is increasing," Brugger and team write.
paras.zh: 布鲁格和团队写道：“由于全球持续发展、世界能源基础设施摆脱化石燃料的转变以及交通基础设施的电气化，对铜等贱金属、稀土元素等关键矿物以及铀等能源矿物的需求正在增加。”

paras.en: The volume of mining waste is expected to increase rapidly, especially as ore grades decrease. Even when uranium isn't the goal of a mine, many rare earth element deposits are tied up with uranium and thorium that go on to enter the mine's waste stream.
paras.zh: 采矿废物量预计将迅速增加，特别是随着矿石品位下降。即使铀不是矿山的目标，许多稀土元素矿床也与铀和钍结合在一起，然后进入矿山的废物流。

paras.en: "As we rapidly scale up operations to meet the unprecedented demand for critical minerals, the volume of mining waste generated globally is going to rise significantly," says environmental microbiologist Santonu Sanyal.
paras.zh: 环境微生物学家 Santonu Sanyal 表示：“随着我们迅速扩大运营规模，以满足对关键矿物前所未有的需求，全球产生的采矿废物量将大幅增加。”

paras.en: "Understanding exactly how these native microbes interact with waste materials is absolutely vital if we want to prevent unseen, long-term environmental contamination and develop the sustainable mine of the future."
paras.zh: “如果我们想要防止看不见的长期环境污染并开发未来的可持续矿山，那么准确了解这些原生微生物如何与废料相互作用绝对至关重要。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Journal of Hazardous Materials.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《危险材料杂志》上。

articles.title: These tiny snakes roll four times faster than they slither

paras.en: These tiny snakes roll four times faster than they slither
paras.zh: 这些小蛇的滚动速度比滑行速度快四倍

paras.en: Acrobatic body movements allow dwarf reedsnakes to keep their heads stable while much of the body rotates rapidly.
paras.zh: 杂技般的身体动作使矮芦苇蛇能够在身体大部分快速旋转的同时保持头部稳定。

paras.en: - Tiny snakes in Southeast Asia have mastered an extraordinary escape technique: rolling across the ground at speeds up to four times faster than ordinary slithering. Scientists discovered that dwarf reedsnakes accomplish this feat through precisely coordinated body movements that allow their bodies to rotate while their heads remain remarkably stable.
paras.zh: - 东南亚的小蛇掌握了一种非凡的逃跑技术：在地面上滚动的速度比普通蛇行的速度快四倍。科学家发现，矮芦苇蛇通过精确协调的身体运动来完成这一壮举，这些运动使它们的身体能够旋转，同时它们的头部保持非常稳定。

paras.en: Tiny snakes found in Southeast Asia have developed an extraordinary way to escape danger. Instead of relying on the familiar side-to-side motion of slithering, dwarf reedsnakes can rapidly roll across the ground, reaching speeds about four times faster than their usual movement.
paras.zh: 东南亚发现的小蛇已经发展出一种非凡的逃离危险的方法。矮芦苇蛇不再依靠熟悉的侧向滑行运动，而是可以在地面上快速滚动，达到比平常运动快四倍左右的速度。

paras.en: Scientists have now uncovered how these small reptiles accomplish such an unusual feat. By studying video recordings captured from multiple angles, researchers discovered that the snakes coordinate their movements with remarkable precision. While the rear portions of their bodies rotate rapidly, their heads remain relatively steady, facing forward and staying at a nearly constant height.
paras.zh: 科学家们现在已经揭示了这些小型爬行动物是如何完成如此不寻常的壮举的。通过研究从多个角度拍摄的视频记录，研究人员发现蛇以惊人的精确度协调它们的动作。当他们身体的后部快速旋转时，他们的头部保持相对稳定，面向前方并保持在几乎恒定的高度。

paras.en: [See link to video after the end of the article.]
paras.zh: 【视频链接见文章末尾。】

paras.en: The findings reveal how an animal can achieve an unexpected form of movement through specialized behavior and body control, even without the physical structures normally needed for rolling.
paras.zh: 研究结果揭示了动物如何通过专门的行为和身体控制来实现意想不到的运动形式，即使没有滚动通常所需的物理结构。

paras.en: Rolling might seem like an effective way to travel quickly, but it presents a major challenge for living creatures.
paras.zh: 滚动似乎是一种快速旅行的有效方式，但它对生物来说是一个重大挑战。

paras.en: A wheel can spin continuously around a fixed axle, allowing it to rotate without disturbing whatever it supports. Animals, however, have no comparable mechanism separating their rotating bodies from their heads.
paras.zh: 轮子可以绕固定轴连续旋转，使其旋转时不会干扰其支撑的任何物体。然而，动物没有类似的机制将旋转的身体与头部分开。

paras.en: If an animal's entire body spins together, its head and sensory organs must also rotate. This can make it difficult to maintain balance, adjust body position, and steer in the intended direction. As rolling speed increases, these problems become even harder to manage.
paras.zh: 如果动物的整个身体一起旋转，它的头部和感觉器官也必须旋转。这可能会导致难以保持平衡、调整身体位置以及转向预期方向。随着轧制速度的增加，这些问题变得更加难以管理。

paras.en: Yet dwarf reedsnakes belonging to the genus Pseudorabdion have found a way around these limitations.
paras.zh: 然而，属于拟蛇属的矮芦苇蛇已经找到了解决这些限制的方法。

paras.en: These small Southeast Asian snakes are among the few animals known to deliberately roll as a means of escaping potential predators. Their unusual behavior has appeared in field guides and was previously documented during a field observation, but scientists had not fully understood the movements that made it possible.
paras.zh: 这些东南亚小蛇是已知的少数几种故意滚动以逃避潜在捕食者的动物之一。它们不寻常的行为已经出现在野外指南中，并且之前在野外观察期间也有记录，但科学家们尚未完全理解使其成为可能的运动。

paras.en: Tiny Snakes Roll Four Times Faster Than They Slither
paras.zh: 小蛇滚动速度比滑行速度快四倍

paras.en: To investigate this remarkable escape strategy, researchers filmed dwarf reedsnakes from several angles and carefully examined how different parts of their bodies moved during rolling.
paras.zh: 为了研究这种非凡的逃生策略，研究人员从多个角度拍摄了矮芦苇蛇，并仔细检查了它们身体不同部位在滚动过程中如何移动。

paras.en: The results revealed impressive speeds. While rolling, the snakes reached peak forward velocities ranging from 1.72 to 3.69 meters per second, approximately four times their maximum speed when moving through lateral undulation, the familiar side-to-side motion used by most snakes.
paras.zh: 结果显示速度令人印象深刻。在滚动时，蛇达到每秒 1.72 至 3.69 米的峰值前进速度，大约是通过横向波动（大多数蛇所熟悉的左右运动）时的最大速度的四倍。

paras.en: Despite traveling so quickly, the snakes were able to follow a narrow racetrack measuring just 20 centimeters across, demonstrating that their rolling movements are not simply uncontrolled tumbling.
paras.zh: 尽管移动速度如此之快，蛇仍然能够沿着直径仅 20 厘米的狭窄跑道行驶，这表明它们的滚动运动不仅仅是不受控制的翻滚。

paras.en: Closer examination of the recordings revealed a surprisingly intricate sequence of movements.
paras.zh: 对录音的仔细检查揭示了一系列令人惊讶的复杂动作。

paras.en: Rather than spinning their entire bodies together, the snakes alternate between rolling on one side and swinging a curved section of their bodies downward beside their heads. The researchers called this downward sweeping movement a "stroke."
paras.zh: 这些蛇不是将整个身体旋转在一起，而是交替在一侧滚动和在头部旁边向下摆动身体的弯曲部分。研究人员将这种向下扫动的运动称为“中风”。

paras.en: During each successive cycle, the side touching the ground switches, and the stroke changes direction from left to right or right to left. By repeating this carefully timed pattern, the snakes generate continuous forward rolling motion.
paras.zh: 在每个连续的循环中，接触地面的一侧会切换，并且行程方向会从左到右或从右到左改变。通过重复这种精心计时的模式，蛇会产生连续的向前滚动运动。

paras.en: The Remarkable Secret Behind Their High-Speed Escape
paras.zh: 他们高速逃跑背后的惊人秘密

paras.en: One of the most surprising discoveries involved what happens to the snakes' heads during these rapid movements.
paras.zh: 最令人惊讶的发现之一涉及蛇的头部在这些快速运动过程中发生的变化。

paras.en: Although the rear portions of their bodies undergo substantial rotation, the snakes keep their heads pointed in the direction they are traveling. Rather than spinning along with the rest of the body, the head remains comparatively stable.
paras.zh: 尽管它们身体的后部发生大幅旋转，但蛇的头部始终指向它们行进的方向。头部保持相对稳定，而不是与身体的其他部分一起旋转。

paras.en: The researchers also found that the snakes maintain a relatively consistent head height above the ground. This stabilization becomes especially noticeable at higher speeds, when the snakes tend to hold their heads elevated and minimize upward and downward movements.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，蛇的头部距地面的高度保持相对一致。这种稳定性在速度较高时变得尤其明显，此时蛇往往会抬起头并尽量减少向上和向下的运动。

paras.en: Keeping the head steady while the rest of the body rotates may help the animals maintain control and navigate effectively during their rapid escapes.
paras.zh: 在身体其他部分旋转时保持头部稳定可能有助于动物在快速逃跑过程中保持控制和有效导航。

paras.en: This ability is particularly remarkable because the snakes accomplish it without a mechanical separation between the rotating and stabilized portions of their bodies.
paras.zh: 这种能力尤其引人注目，因为蛇在其身体的旋转部分和稳定部分之间没有机械分离的情况下实现了这一能力。

paras.en: What Rolling Snakes Reveal About Evolution
paras.zh: 滚动的蛇揭示了进化论

paras.en: The discovery demonstrates how sophisticated coordination can allow animals to overcome physical limitations that might otherwise make certain types of movement impractical.
paras.zh: 这一发现表明，复杂的协调性如何能够让动物克服身体限制，否则某些类型的运动可能变得不切实际。

paras.en: Although dwarf reedsnakes lack anything resembling a wheel's axle, they effectively divide their bodies into regions with different functions. Much of the body performs the powerful rotational movements needed for propulsion, while the head remains stabilized to support controlled travel.
paras.zh: 尽管矮芦苇蛇缺乏类似轮轴的东西，但它们有效地将身体划分为具有不同功能的区域。身体的大部分执行推进所需的强大旋转运动，而头部保持稳定以支持受控行进。

paras.en: This unusual strategy allows the snakes to combine speed, directional control, and rapid body rotation in a way that would be difficult to predict from their anatomy alone.
paras.zh: 这种不寻常的策略使蛇能够将速度、方向控制和快速的身体旋转结合起来，而这种方式仅凭其解剖结构很难预测。

paras.en: More broadly, the findings highlight an important principle of animal evolution: physical structure does not necessarily determine the full range of movements an animal can perform. Innovative behaviors and precise muscular coordination can open up entirely new possibilities, allowing creatures to accomplish feats that their body shapes might initially suggest are impossible.
paras.zh: 更广泛地说，这些发现强调了动物进化的一个重要原则：身体结构不一定决定动物可以执行的全部运动。创新的行为和精确的肌肉协调可以开辟全新的可能性，使生物能够完成其体型最初可能认为不可能的壮举。

paras.zh: 资料由东邦大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun

paras.en: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
paras.zh: 天文学家在太阳上方发现了一个神秘的磁网

paras.en: - National Institutes of Natural Sciences
paras.zh: - 国立自然科学研究所

paras.en: - The Sunâs seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world. Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sunâs surface. They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.
paras.zh: - 太阳看似平静的区域隐藏着一个极其复杂的磁场世界。科学家们利用地球上空的气球望远镜发现了太阳大气层中编织的精致的线状磁性结构，这些结构显然是由太阳表面的扭曲运动形成的。他们还绘制了高耸的太阳能材料射流内部的磁场图，揭示了这些磁场如何随高度变化。

paras.en: Scientists have uncovered a surprisingly complex network of magnetic structures hidden above regions of the Sun that appear relatively calm. Using the Sunrise-III solar observatory, which traveled high into Earth's stratosphere aboard a balloon in 2024, an international research team led by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) discovered intricate, thread-like magnetic features that had previously been difficult to observe.
paras.zh: 科学家们发现了隐藏在看似相对平静的太阳区域上方的一个令人惊讶的复杂磁结构网络。由日本国家天文台 (NAOJ) 领导的一个国际研究小组利用 2024 年乘坐气球进入地球平流层高空的 Sunrise-III 太阳观测站，发现了以前难以观察到的复杂的线状磁性特征​​。

paras.en: The findings reveal that even the Sun's seemingly quiet regions contain elaborate magnetic structures. They also offer new clues to how energy travels upward through the solar atmosphere and contributes to its heating.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，即使是太阳看似安静的区域也含有复杂的磁性结构。它们还为能量如何穿过太阳大气层向上传播并促进其加热提供了新的线索。

paras.en: A Hidden Web of Magnetic Threads Above the Sun
paras.zh: 太阳上方隐藏的磁线网

paras.en: Sunrise-III detected numerous thin, elongated magnetic structures woven into a larger network of magnetic fields above a quiet region of the Sun. This network, known as the magnetic canopy, extends through the chromosphere, a layer of the solar atmosphere located above the Sun's visible surface.
paras.zh: Sunrise-III 检测到许多细长的磁性结构，这些结构编织成太阳安静区域上方更大的磁场网络。这个网络被称为磁冠，延伸穿过色球层，色球层是位于太阳可见表面上方的太阳大气层。

paras.en: The canopy develops as magnetic fields concentrated at the solar surface (photosphere) spread outward and arch upward into the chromosphere (chromosphere). Rather than forming a relatively smooth, uniformly expanding structure, however, the new observations reveal that the canopy contains many narrow, thread-like features.
paras.zh: 当集中在太阳表面（光球层）的磁场向外扩散并向上拱入色球层（色球层）时，冠层就会形成。然而，新的观察结果表明，树冠并没有形成相对光滑、均匀膨胀的结构，而是包含许多狭窄的线状特征。

paras.en: To investigate how these structures form, researchers used computer simulations that successfully reproduced the patterns recorded by Sunrise-III. The results suggest that movements on the solar surface twist magnetic field lines, creating the intricate structures observed higher in the atmosphere.
paras.zh: 为了研究这些结构是如何形成的，研究人员使用计算机模拟成功地再现了 Sunrise-III 记录的模式。结果表明，太阳表面的运动扭曲了磁场线，从而形成了在大气层高层观察到的复杂结构。

paras.en: The observatory also examined another quiet region near the solar limb (visible edge of the Sun). There, it measured magnetic fields within spicules, narrow jets of solar material that extend upward from the surface. These observations revealed how the distribution of magnetic fields changes with increasing height above the Sun's visible edge.
paras.zh: 天文台还检查了太阳边缘（太阳可见边缘）附近的另一个安静区域。在那里，它测量了针状体（从表面向上延伸的太阳能材料的狭窄射流）内的磁场。这些观测揭示了磁场分布如何随着太阳可见边缘上方高度的增加而变化。

paras.en: Why the Sun's Quiet Regions Are Difficult to Study
paras.zh: 为什么太阳的安静区域难以研究

paras.en: Although the Sun is constantly active, much of its surface lacks prominent features such as sunspots. Scientists describe these comparatively inactive areas as "quiet." They cover most of the Sun, making them especially important for understanding how our star behaves.
paras.zh: 尽管太阳一直很活跃，但它的大部分表面缺乏诸如太阳黑子之类的显着特征。科学家将这些相对不活跃的区域描述为“安静”。它们覆盖了太阳的大部分区域，这使得它们对于了解我们的恒星的行为尤其重要。

paras.en: However, quiet does not mean magnetically inactive. These regions contain magnetic fields that are generally weaker than those found in more active areas of the Sun. Their subtle structures are difficult to measure, especially with telescopes on the ground, where turbulence in Earth's atmosphere can blur fine details.
paras.zh: 然而，安静并不意味着磁力不活跃。这些区域的磁场通常比太阳更活跃区域的磁场弱。它们微妙的结构很难测量，尤其是使用地面望远镜，地球大气层的湍流会模糊精细的细节。

paras.en: Sunrise-III was designed to overcome this obstacle by carrying a powerful solar telescope far above most of the atmosphere.
paras.zh: Sunrise-III 的设计是为了克服这一障碍，它携带了一个远高于大气层的强大太阳望远镜。

paras.en: A Balloon-Borne Telescope Reveals New Solar Details
paras.zh: 气球望远镜揭示了太阳的新细节

paras.en: Sunrise-III is an international research project built around a 1-meter telescope carried by a high-altitude balloon. During its 2024 mission, the observatory floated approximately 35 kilometers (about 22 miles) above Earth in the stratosphere, where atmospheric interference is greatly reduced.
paras.zh: Sunrise-III 是一个国际研究项目，围绕高空气球携带的 1 米望远镜而建。在 2024 年的任务期间，天文台漂浮在距地球约 35 公里（约 22 英里）的平流层中，大气干扰大大减少。

paras.en: This elevated vantage point allowed the telescope to capture exceptionally detailed measurements of the Sun's magnetic fields.
paras.zh: 这个较高的有利位置使望远镜能够捕获太阳磁场的极其详细的测量结果。

paras.en: The balloon's gondola carried three scientific instruments developed through contributions from different countries. One of these was SCIP (Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared spectroPolarimeter), a near-infrared instrument developed under NAOJ's leadership.
paras.zh: 气球的吊舱载有三台由不同国家贡献开发的科学仪器。其中之一是 SCIP（日出色球红外光谱偏振计），这是一种在 NAOJ 的领导下开发的近红外仪器。

paras.en: SCIP is designed to measure magnetic fields continuously across different layers of the solar atmosphere, from the photosphere to the chromosphere. This capability allowed researchers to examine how magnetic structures extend and change with altitude rather than studying only a single layer.
paras.zh: SCIP 旨在连续测量太阳大气不同层（从光球层到色球层）的磁场。这种能力使研究人员能够检查磁性结构如何随高度延伸和变化，而不是仅研究单层。

paras.en: New Clues to How the Sun's Atmosphere Is Heated
paras.zh: 关于太阳大气如何加热的新线索

paras.en: By observing from the stratosphere, Sunrise-III provided researchers with an unusually detailed picture of magnetic fields above the Sun's quiet regions. Its measurements revealed that the chromosphere contains far more intricate magnetic structures than a simple expanding canopy would suggest.
paras.zh: 通过从平流层进行观测，“日出三号”为研究人员提供了太阳安静区域上方磁场异常详细的图像。它的测量结果表明，色球层包含的磁性结构比简单的膨胀冠层所暗示的要复杂得多。

paras.en: Understanding these structures could help scientists investigate how energy generated by motions near the solar surface is transferred into higher layers of the atmosphere.
paras.zh: 了解这些结构可以帮助科学家研究太阳表面附近运动产生的能量如何转移到大气的高层。

paras.en: The discovery offers an important step toward explaining how magnetic activity contributes to heating the Sun's atmosphere, including in regions that appear calm when viewed from afar.
paras.zh: 这一发现为解释磁活动如何导致太阳大气层加热（包括从远处观察时显得平静的区域）迈出了重要的一步。

articles.title: Scientists propose a way to detect dangerous “mirror life” before it exists

paras.en: Scientists propose a way to detect dangerous âmirror lifeâ before it exists
paras.zh: 科学家提出了一种在危险的“镜像生命”存在之前检测到它的方法

paras.en: - Scientists have proposed a way to detect âmirror life,â a hypothetical form of life that could pose serious risks to humans, animals, and ecosystems if artificially created. Using special fluorescent molecules and a type of polarized light also used in 3D movie technology, researchers believe they could distinguish ordinary organisms from their mirror-image counterparts.
paras.zh: - 科学家提出了一种检测“镜像生命”的方法，这是一种假设的生命形式，如果人工创造，可能会对人类、动物和生态系统造成严重风险。研究人员相信，利用特殊的荧光分子和一种也用于 3D 电影技术的偏振光，他们可以将普通生物体与镜像生物区分开来。

paras.en: Scientists have proposed what they believe is the first way to detect "mirror life," a hypothetical form of life built from molecules that are reversed versions of those found in living organisms on Earth.
paras.zh: 科学家们提出了他们认为是检测“镜像生命”的第一种方法，这是一种由分子构成的假设生命形式，这些分子是地球上生物体中发现的分子的反向版本。

paras.en: Researchers from the University of Strathclyde and Durham University have developed a proposed detection technique that uses molecules capable of emitting light with distinct left and right-handed properties. By analyzing these light signals, scientists may eventually be able to distinguish conventional organisms from their mirror-image counterparts.
paras.zh: 斯特拉斯克莱德大学和杜伦大学的研究人员开发了一种拟议的检测技术，该技术使用能够发射具有明显左旋和右旋特性的光的分子。通过分析这些光信号，科学家最终可能能够区分传统生物和镜像生物。

paras.en: Although mirror life does not currently exist, some experts consider its potential creation a serious biological safety concern. These artificial organisms could behave in unpredictable ways when interacting with Earth's ecosystems and might evade certain natural defenses that protect people, animals, and plants.
paras.zh: 尽管镜像生命目前并不存在，但一些专家认为其潜在的产生会带来严重的生物安全问题。这些人造生物体在与地球生态系统相互作用时可能会以不可预测的方式表现，并可能逃避某些保护人类、动物和植物的自然防御。

paras.en: The likelihood of mirror life emerging is considered low, but its possible consequences could be severe enough to justify developing detection methods in advance.
paras.zh: 镜像生命出现的可能性被认为很低，但其可能的后果可能非常严重，足以证明提前开发检测方法是合理的。

paras.en: Why Mirror Life Could Pose a Biological Threat
paras.zh: 为什么镜像生命可能构成生物威胁

paras.en: Concerns about mirror life have prompted scientists to recommend restrictions on research intended to produce organisms capable of reproducing using mirror-image biological molecules.
paras.zh: 对镜像生命的担忧促使科学家建议限制旨在生产能够利用镜像生物分子繁殖的生物体的研究。

paras.en: The potential dangers have also attracted attention from governments and international organizations, including the UK Government Office for Science and the United Nations Secretary General's Scientific Advisory Board.
paras.zh: 潜在的危险也引起了各国政府和国际组织的关注，包括英国政府科学办公室和联合国秘书长的科学顾问委员会。

paras.en: The underlying science involves a property of molecules known as chirality, often described as molecular "handedness." Just as a person's left and right hands are mirror images that cannot be perfectly aligned, some molecules can exist in two forms that have identical chemical components but different three-dimensional arrangements.
paras.zh: 其基础科学涉及分子的一种称为手性的特性，通常被描述为分子的“手性”。正如人的左右手是镜像一样，无法完美对齐，有些分子可以以化学成分相同但三维排列不同的两种形式存在。

paras.en: These subtle structural differences can have major biological consequences. Two mirror-image versions of a molecule contain the same atoms connected in the same order, yet the human body may respond to them very differently. For example, one form of a medication could successfully treat a disease, while its mirror-image counterpart might be ineffective or even harmful.
paras.zh: 这些微妙的结构差异可能会产生重大的生物学后果。分子的两个镜像版本包含以相同顺序连接的相同原子，但人体对它们的反应可能截然不同。例如，一种药物可以成功治疗某种疾病，而其镜像对应物可能无效甚至有害。

paras.en: Scientists are concerned that organisms assembled from reversed biological building blocks could interact with existing life in unexpected ways.
paras.zh: 科学家担心，由反向生物构件组装而成的生物体可能会以意想不到的方式与现有生命相互作用。

paras.en: Importantly, the researchers emphasize that mirror life remains entirely hypothetical. Their proposed detection method is intended as a precaution, not a response to an existing biological threat.
paras.zh: 重要的是，研究人员强调，镜像生命仍然完全是假设的。他们提出的检测方法旨在作为预防措施，而不是对现有生物威胁的响应。

paras.en: How Light Could Reveal Mirror-Image Life
paras.zh: 光如何揭示镜像生命

paras.en: The proposed approach relies on a phenomenon called circularly polarized luminescence (CPL), which can reveal the molecular handedness, or chirality, of certain substances and biological structures.
paras.zh: 所提出的方法依赖于一种称为圆偏振发光（CPL）的现象，它可以揭示某些物质和生物结构的分子旋向性或手性。

paras.en: Light can exhibit different polarization patterns, including forms that rotate in opposite directions. By studying these patterns, researchers can obtain information about the three-dimensional arrangement of molecules.
paras.zh: 光可以表现出不同的偏振模式，包括沿相反方向旋转的形式。通过研究这些图案，研究人员可以获得有关分子三维排列的信息。

paras.en: The underlying concept has a surprisingly familiar application: the polarized light technology used in modern 3D movie glasses to create the illusion of depth.
paras.zh: 其基本概念有一个令人惊讶的熟悉应用：现代 3D 电影眼镜中使用的偏振光技术，可产生深度幻觉。

paras.en: The research, published in Royal Society Open Science under the title 'Circularly Polarized Luminescence (CPL) as a Contingency Assay for "Mirror Life" Bio-Hazards', was led by Dr. Lewis MacKenzie of the University of Strathclyde's Department of Pure and Applied Chemistry, working with Professor Robert Pal of Durham University.
paras.zh: 这项研究发表在《皇家学会开放科学》上，题为“圆偏振发光（CPL）作为“镜像生命”生物危害的应急分析”，由斯特拉斯克莱德大学纯粹与应用化学系的 Lewis MacKenzie 博士领导，与杜伦大学的 Robert Pal 教授合作。

paras.en: Dr. MacKenzie said: "We don't expect mirror life to appear tomorrow, but if it did arise, the consequences could be severe, and it makes sense to develop detection methods before they are needed. Professor Pal and I had been working on CPL technologies before recent concerns became prominent, and guarding against mirror life was a clear fit for our research."
paras.zh: 麦肯齐博士说：“我们预计镜子生命不会在明天出现，但如果它真的出现，后果可能会很严重，在需要它们之前开发检测方法是有意义的。在最近的担忧变得突出之前，帕尔教授和我一直在研究 CPL 技术，防范镜子生命显然适合我们的研究。”

paras.en: A Molecular Fingerprint for Detecting Mirror Life
paras.zh: 用于检测镜子寿命的分子指纹

paras.en: To identify a possible mirror organism, the researchers suggest using specialized fluorescent probes that attach to particular structures inside cells.
paras.zh: 为了识别可能的镜像生物，研究人员建议使用附着在细胞内特定结构上的专门荧光探针。

paras.en: Once bound to their targets, these probes would generate characteristic CPL signals. Scientists could analyze the resulting patterns to determine whether a biological sample contains the molecular handedness associated with ordinary terrestrial life or its reversed equivalent.
paras.zh: 一旦与目标结合，这些探针就会产生特征性的 CPL 信号。科学家可以分析由此产生的模式，以确定生物样本是否包含与普通陆地生命相关的分子旋向性或其相反的等价物。

paras.en: In effect, the light signals could serve as a molecular fingerprint, revealing differences that might otherwise be difficult to identify.
paras.zh: 实际上，光信号可以充当分子指纹，揭示否则可能难以识别的差异。

paras.en: However, relying on a single fluorescent probe could produce misleading results. To improve reliability and reduce the risk of false readings, the team proposes combining several probes designed to recognize different cellular structures.
paras.zh: 然而，依赖单一荧光探针可能会产生误导性的结果。为了提高可靠性并降低错误读数的风险，该团队建议结合几种旨在识别不同细胞结构的探针。

paras.en: By examining multiple signals together, researchers hope to develop a more dependable way to distinguish conventional organisms from hypothetical mirror life.
paras.zh: 通过同时检查多个信号，研究人员希望开发出一种更可靠的方法来区分传统生物和假设的镜像生命。

paras.en: Testing the Technology Without Creating Mirror Organisms
paras.zh: 在不创建镜像生物的情况下测试技术

paras.en: One important advantage of the proposed technique is that scientists could begin investigating and refining it using ordinary biological samples. There would be no need to manufacture mirror organisms simply to explore whether the underlying detection principles work.
paras.zh: 该技术的一个重要优点是科学家可以使用普通生物样本开始研究和改进它。没有必要仅仅为了探索基本检测原理是否有效而制造镜像生物体。

paras.en: The researchers also believe the method could eventually be incorporated into several types of scientific equipment, potentially allowing mirror-life screening in different environments.
paras.zh: 研究人员还相信，该方法最终可能会被纳入多种类型的科学设备中，从而有可能在不同的环境中进行镜像生命筛选。

paras.en: Professor Pal has already demonstrated laboratory-scale CPL detection technologies involving microscopes, cameras, and biological cell plate readers, which are instruments commonly used to examine large numbers of cell samples.
paras.zh: Pal 教授已经展示了实验室规模的 CPL 检测技术，包括显微镜、相机和生物细胞读板器，这些都是检查大量细胞样本的常用仪器。

paras.en: However, the complete detection method specifically designed to identify mirror life has not yet been experimentally demonstrated. Further research will be necessary to determine whether the proposed approach can reliably distinguish between different forms of molecular handedness in biological samples.
paras.zh: 然而，专门设计用于识别镜子寿命的完整检测方法尚未得到实验证明。需要进一步的研究来确定所提出的方法是否能够可靠地区分生物样本中不同形式的分子惯用手。

paras.en: Professor Pal added: "CPL detection relies on the same fundamental concept that allows modern 3D cinema glasses to create a stereoscopic image.
paras.zh: Pal 教授补充道：“CPL 检测依赖于现代 3D 电影眼镜创建立体图像的相同基本概念。

paras.en: "This CPL detection approach can be adapted to many types of systems for analysis of cells, including biological plate readers, microscopes, and cameras. This means our mirror life assay approach could be generalized to many environments depending on end user needs."
paras.zh: “这种 CPL 检测方法可以适应多种类型的细胞分析系统，包括生物读板机、显微镜和相机。这意味着我们的镜寿命测定方法可以根据最终用户的需求推广到许多环境。”

paras.en: Materials provided by https://www.strath.ac.uk/. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由 https://www.strath.ac.uk/ 提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Lewis E. MacKenzie, Dominic J. Black, Robert Pal. Circularly polarized luminescence as a contingency assay for âmirror lifeâ bio-hazards. Royal Society Open Science, 2026; 13 (10) DOI: 10.1098/rsos.260921
paras.zh: - 刘易斯·E·麦肯齐、多米尼克·J·布莱克、罗伯特·帕尔。圆偏振发光作为“镜像生命”生物危害的应急测定。英国皇家学会开放科学，2026； 13 (10) DOI：10.1098/rsos.260921

articles.title: Rocket Lab launches 3 'Hawk' satellites to orbit to gather signals intelligence
articles.author: Mike Wall

paras.en: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23).
paras.zh: 今天（10 月 23 日）火箭实验室将三颗私人信号情报卫星发射到轨道。

paras.en: The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand).
paras.zh: 今天美国东部时间凌晨 3 点 11 分（格林威治标准时间 0711；新西兰当地时间晚上 8 点 11 分），该任务搭乘电子火箭从火箭实验室新西兰发射场升空。

paras.en: The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around."
paras.zh: Electron 为总部位于弗吉尼亚州的 HawkEye 360​​ 公司携带了三颗“Hawk”卫星，这解释了火箭实验室给该任务起的名字：“我们不是霍金”。

paras.en: If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.
paras.zh: 如果一切按计划进行，三架“鹰”将被部署到高度 323 英里（520 公里）的近地轨道 (LEO)。一旦到达那里并投入使用，卫星将扫描全球的射频（RF）辐射。

paras.en: "Operating in clusters of three, HawkEye 360's satellites collect signal data from across the RF spectrum for maritime tracking, GNSS jamming detection, radar monitoring, communications mapping and space defense," Rocket Lab wrote in a mission description.
paras.zh: 火箭实验室在任务描述中写道：“HawkEye 360​​ 卫星以三颗集群的形式运行，从整个射频频谱收集信号数据，用于海上跟踪、GNSS 干扰检测、雷达监控、通信测绘和太空防御。”

paras.en: HawkEye 360 provides this data to the U.S. government and its allies "to enable faster, better decision-making," according to the company. "Our space-based collection, proprietary signal processing and AI-powered analytics transform knowledge of the RF spectrum into a strategic advantage."
paras.zh: 据该公司称，HawkEye 360​​ 向美国政府及其盟友提供这些数据，“以实现更快、更好的决策”。 “我们的天基收集、专有信号处理和人工智能分析将射频频谱知识转化为战略优势。”

paras.en: HawkEye 360's first satellites launched in 2018, and the company has now sent nearly 50 of them to LEO. The most recent Hawk launch before "We're Not Hawking Around" came just two days ago; three of the satellites went up on SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission.
paras.zh: HawkEye 360​​ 的第一颗卫星于 2018 年发射，该公司目前已向近地轨道发射了近 50 颗卫星。在“We're Not Hawking around”之前的最新一次 Hawk 发射就在两天前；其中三颗卫星执行了 SpaceX 的 Bandwagon-5 乘车共享任务。

paras.en: "We're Not Hawking Around "was Rocket Lab's 98th launch to date and its 19th of 2026 so far. Sixteen of this year's flights have been performed by the two-stage, 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron. The other three have been conducted by HASTE, a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test technologies in a hypersonic flight environment.
paras.zh: “We're Not Hawking around”是 Rocket Lab 迄今为止的第 98 次发射，也是 2026 年迄今为止的第 19 次发射。今年的 16 次飞行是由 59 英尺高（18 米）的两级 Electron 执行的。另外三项是由 HASTE 进行的，HASTE 是 Electron 的亚轨道变体，允许客户在高超音速飞行环境中测试技术。

paras.en: Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. To find out what his latest project is, you can follow Michael on Twitter.
paras.zh: Michael Wall 是 Space.com 的太空飞行和技术编辑，于 2010 年加入该团队。他主要报道人类和机器人太空飞行、军事太空和系外行星，但以涉足太空艺术领域而闻名。他关于寻找外星生命的书《Out There》于 2018 年 11 月 13 日出版。在成为科普作家之前，迈克尔曾是一名爬行动物学家和野生动物生物学家。他拥有博士学位。澳大利亚悉尼大学进化生物学博士学位、亚利桑那大学学士学位以及加州大学圣克鲁斯分校科学写作研究生证书。要了解他的最新项目是什么，您可以在 Twitter 上关注 Michael。
