articles.title: The most beautiful sections of China's Great Wall

paras.en: Editor’s Note: Monthly Ticket is a CNN Travel series that spotlights some of the most fascinating topics in the travel world. In September, we’re celebrating superlatives as we look at some of the world’s biggest, tallest and most expensive attractions and destinations.
Having lived in Beijing for almost 12 years, I’ve had plenty of time to travel widely in China.
I’ve visited more than 100 cities, not to mention countless towns and villages throughout the mainland’s 31 provinces.

Looking back, I’ve come to realize it was my frequent visits to different parts of the Great Wall in Beijing that were a driving force behind my desire to explore the rest of the country and, along with it, the many sections of wall that lie outside the capital’s boundaries.

Work on the Great Wall began more than 2,500 years ago, its origins dating back to China’s Spring and Autumn Period of around 770 BCE to 476 BCE. Various sections were added in subsequent eras as competing dynasties and factions sought to exert their control.
Work eventually stopped in the 17th century.
Though not a single, unbroken structure, the wall spans over 21,000 kilometers, winding through 15 provinces, 97 prefectures and 404 counties.
And while certain sections have been incredibly popular among tourists, many parts have slipped into obscurity, disrepair and sometimes oblivion.

Whether you’re planning to visit the Great Wall for the first time or the 50th, the following destinations are sure to make your trip to China even more worthwhile. (Check out the above video for dramatic aerial footage of some of these amazing sites.)
The Great Wall is not simply a brick and mortar bulwark; in certain places, towers on jagged mountain peaks, fortress towns or even wide rivers count as sections of “wall.”

The Turtle City, built in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) as part of the Great Wall’s “Yellow River Defense Line,” was completed in 1608 and was home to around 2,000 infantrymen and 500 cavalry units during peak use.
Today, this fortress city is located in the Sitan Township of Jingtai County in north central Gansu province.
While there aren’t many real turtles in the “Turtle City,” the garrison town got its nickname due to its unique shape.

The south gate acts as the head and the west and east gates as the flippers. The town’s oval wall is the body, while the north gate acts as its tail. As one of the most well-preserved and truly authentic walled cities left in China today, it’s definitely worth your time.
Staying in the Jingtai County center is recommended. The ancient city is only a 30-minute cab ride from your lodgings, so you can visit whenever the light is best for photos.

When in Jingtai, try local specialties such as the five Buddha tofu and the Jingtai cold mixed noodles – both are spicy vegetarian dishes. A walk through the sprawling night market in Jingtai County People’s Square, which boasts more than 50 snack stalls, is also recommended for adventurous foodies.

Getting there: Lanzhou, the capital of Gansu province, has a major international airport and high-speed train connections from many cities in China. The drive to Yongtai Turtle City from downtown Lanzhou takes about 2.5 hours (195 kilometers). From Lanzhou Zhongchuan Airport, it’s only 1.5 hours (125 kilometers).
Mutianyu and Jiankou are two parts of the same Stone Dragon – two contiguous sections of the Great Wall that together stretch for roughly 25 kilometers along Beijing’s mountaintops.

Historical records show that millions of men spent centuries constructing the Great Wall. Stand atop the wall at either Mutianyu or Jiankou, and you’ll begin to comprehend the gravity of this statement.
These two sections are arguably the two most classic examples of Ming Dynasty Great Wall surviving today, and climbing either is guaranteed to be a life-changing experience.
Mutianyu is the best portion of the “tourist wall.” Restored in the 1980s, it’s very commercial but also superbly beautiful. Visitors not up for the hike can take a cable car to the top.

To the west of Mutianyu, Jiankou is colloquially known as the “wild wall” – no ticket needed and not commercialized. That being said, as of 2020, hiking at Jiankou has become somewhat frowned upon by the local government because of safety concerns.
Mutianyu and Jiankou are less than a 90-minute drive (without traffic) from downtown Beijing, yet it’s highly recommended to enjoy a night in the countryside if time allows.

Jiankou can be accessed via Xizhazi village; if dates align, you might even be able to spend a few days with William Lindesay, world-renowned Great Wall historian, and his wonderful family at The Barracks, their wall-side courtyard home.
For lodgings around Mutianyu, The Brickyard is a superbly comfortable choice.
In fall and spring, shades of the wall’s gray brick contrast with nature’s vibrant colors. Peak autumn foliage and spring cherry blossoms provide stunning backdrops for photos.
For winter sports enthusiasts, there’s skiing and skating next to the Wall at locations not far from Mutianyu.

Getting to Mutianyu: Restrictions on applying for temporary driving licenses in China were relaxed in September 2019, so renting a car as a foreign tourist is entirely possible. (International driving licenses are not accepted in China.)
You can also hire a car with a driver for the day or take the Mutianyu Special Tourism Bus from the Dongzhimen Wai Bus Station.

Getting to Jiankou: Renting a car or booking private transport is recommended. As Xizhazi is a small village, buses are scarce so it can take up to five hours to get there by public transport, as opposed to 90 minutes by car.
Bataizi village sits just inside the Motianling section of the Great Wall and is home to the ruins of a Gothic church built in 1876 under the direction of a German missionary.
The church has been damaged and repaired numerous times in its nearly 150-year history; the bell tower is the only part still standing.
The juxtaposition of its ruins against the rammed-earth Great Wall makes Bataizi a unique place to spend a morning or afternoon.

After finishing your hike along the wall and visiting the church ruins, drop in to the village’s “new” church to say hello to Father Pan; if you speak Chinese, he can answer any questions about the village’s long connection with Catholicism.
Besides Bataizi, Datong should also be on your tourist map; visiting the Yungang Grottoes (a UNESCO world heritage site) and the Hengshan Hanging Temple will make your trip even more memorable.
Late summer is an ideal time to visit Bataizi, as you’ll see a wonderful contrast between the Great Wall and the lush green hills.

Getting there: Bataizi village is 80 kilometers west of Datong, one of Shanxi province’s largest and most famous cities. Zuoyun County is only 22 kilometers away from Bataizi – about a 35-minute drive.
Datong is easily accessible by plane or high-speed train from other cities in China; a taxi from downtown Datong to Bataizi should cost roughly 300 yuan (about $43).
Alternatively, you can make your way to Zuoyun County by bus then hop in a taxi.

In Datong, luxury seekers will want to head for the five-star Yunzhong Traditional Courtyard Hotel. Zuoyun County has one hotel that can accept foreigners: Zuoyun Jinshan International Hotel. Both can be found on popular hotel booking sites.
Laoniuwan (aka the Old Ox Bend Great Wall)
As the locals say, Laoniuwan is where the Great Wall and the mighty Yellow River shake hands.
The Laoniuwan Fortress was built in 1467, while the most famous tower of the Great Wall in this area, Wanghe Tower (literally meaning river-watching tower), was constructed in 1544.
Laoniuwan village is located in Pianguan County, part of Xinzhou city in Shanxi province, just across the river from Inner Mongolia.

Late summer or early fall is a great time to visit, as you’ll avoid the potentially dangerous mountain roads during spring rainstorms, or being uncomfortably cold in a place without great infrastructure.
Along the Great Wall, there are only a few places where it meets bodies of water; of all those, this is the most stunning.
A boat ride along the river is highly recommended. You’ll be able to soak in the natural beauty of the Yellow River Gorge while marveling at the steadfast resolve of these ancient architects.

Getting there: Laoniuwan is difficult to get to by public transportation. The best option is to rent or book a car to take you from Datong to Laoniuwan via Bataizi – this way, you’ll be able to see two incredible locations along the Great Wall in one trip.

Pianguan is the nearest city, about one hour away. Pianguan does not have a train station or an airport. The only option is to arrive by bus. Shuozhou, 140 kilometers from Laoniuwan, has an airport opening later this year.
Construction on the Great Wall in Simatai began in 1373. It was expanded and reinforced periodically throughout the Ming Dynasty.
The Fairy Tower is one of the best-known towers of the wall at Simatai but also one of the least visited due to how difficult it is to access.

Instead, aim to take in incredible views of the Fairy Tower from Wangjing Tower (just a few hundred meters away). It’s a journey that will satiate even the most adventurous hikers, yet can be done without any ropes, ladders or other essential safety gear.

As with a visit to Mutianyu/Jiankou, this section of wall is guaranteed to deliver stunning views any time of year. My only suggestion is to wait for a clear day (usually visibility is great the day after it rains or snows), as the view from Wangjing Tower is unobstructed in every direction.

The hike to the Fairy Tower will leave you in awe of the Northern Barbarians’ supposed determination to reach the capital; the mountains are nearly impassable on foot, let alone by horse, with sheer cliff faces on either side.
It makes for absolutely world-class hiking and an interesting history lesson.

Five-star lodgings are available at Hobo Farm; they also have an incredible restaurant that serves delicious Western and Chinese fare. For 4.5 star lodgings with a lower price tag, try Yatou’s Homestay. Both can be found on major hotel booking sites.
Getting there: Both the Fairy Tower and Wangjing Tower should be accessed via Tangjiazhai village, located in Beijing’s Miyun district.
Tangjiazhai village is 140 kilometers from downtown Beijing, depending on your route. Booking a private car from the city is probably the most time-effective way to get there.
You can also take a high-speed train from Beijing Station to Miyun district and switch to a bus or taxi from there.
Constructed during the reign of Emperor Jiajing (1507-1567), this single-wall section stands seven meters tall in some spots – no small feat considering it was made by piling stones.
It’s located just across the road from the town of Dushikou, in Chicheng in Hebei province.
The piled-stone wall at Dushikou is unique, as many other sections of the Great Wall close to Beijing were constructed using kiln-fired bricks.

Dushikou is best visited in the summer, specifically July and August, when the rolling hills of the surrounding grasslands are peak green. Cool evenings make for perfect outdoor barbecue/bonfire weather.
You’ll be able to find clean and comfortable farmhouse lodgings in Dushikou town; alternatively, Chicheng, 45 minutes away, has a range of hotels to choose from.

Lamb skewers and roast leg of lamb are specialties in these parts, as this part of Hebei is very close to the border with Inner Mongolia. Noodle lovers should also try the local oat noodles, which are delicious.

Getting there: Thanks to all the infrastructure built for the 2022 Winter Olympics, the drive to Dushikou has been shortened by almost two hours. If you prefer not to drive, hop on a bus to Chicheng from the Liuliqiao Transport Hub in Beijing and take a 45-minute taxi ride to Dushikou.
Note that public transportation will take one or two hours longer than private car.

articles.title: Stephen A Smith doubles down on Trump dinner, challenges critics by asking, 'What the f--- are you doing?'

paras.en: Stephen A. Smith doubled down on defending his meeting with President Donald Trump during an episode of his "Straight Shooter" show on Thursday, challenging his critics by asking, "What the f--- are you doing?"

Smith said during the show he wanted to bring several issues to Trump's attention, but his top priority was to tell the president, "With the squashing of DEI initiatives, it's essentially had a different kind of effect. It's discouraged CEOs of corporations in the private sector to be philanthropic and charitable with their money and give to HBCUs because they're fearful it will be perceived as a DEI initiative being exercised by them."

"I needed the president to speak out against that, and he said he didn't think about that and that is something that he was going to tackle, not to mention the fact he followed up with a call to assure me that's exactly what he was going to tackle in a matter of days when he meets with these HBCU officials. Now I don't know what's going to happen, but I tried, as I always have and as I always will," Smith said.
Smith met with Trump, comedian Bill Maher and musician Kid Rock at the White House on Oct. 15.

"All of these folks that are complaining about me showing up to the White House with Bill Maher, what the f--- are you doing? Have you done anything? Are you doing anything? I'm sorry for cussing. I don't mean to, apologizing to the executives at SiriusXM, but damn it. Sometimes we do stuff on the air that we do off the air. This is ridiculous. I mean, it's just, it's never enough," Smith argued.
Smith repeatedly criticized comedian D.L. Hughley during the show, after Hughley questioned Smith's meeting with Trump on the "Uncertain" podcast.

"Why is it that Trump feels so comfortable talking to you when he's shown an aversion to people that challenge him?" Hughley asked during the discussion, as he and his co-hosts criticized Smith for sitting down with the president. "If you challenge him, that's it. Why is it? It isn't that where Stephen A. Smith finds himself his positions, it is that why are people that have a disdain for us so comfortable around you?"
"I think that it says something about you when the people who hate us like you," Hughley added. "Why is it the people that hate my heroes love you?"

Smith criticized Hughley over his comments, saying, "I'm sick and tired of people b----ing and moaning about what needs to be done in our community, but when somebody is actually trying to take steps to do something about it in our own small way, we selling out. We this, we that. What you doing? What you doing? It's a rhetorical question 'cause we know the answer ain't nothing but b----ing."
Smith also defended his Trump meeting during an appearance on "The View" on Wednesday. He told the co-hosts he would not apologize for it.
Co-host Sunny Hostin asked Smith, "He has this history of racial bias that is so clear. Did you think meeting with him, that you got anywhere?"

"I don't know. We'll find out, but he’s the president of the United States, and I’ll be damned if I’m not going to try," he said. "And the reality is I’m just speaking from a constitutional perspective in that regard."
He repeatedly argued that Trump would remain in office until 2028 and that people needed to deal with it.

"You’re going to have to deal with him," he continued. "And when it comes to getting things done, I’m all about exhausting every means and every measure to try to do what’s in the best interest of our community. I’m not apologizing for that to anybody."

"Stephen A. Smith and Bill Maher, along with John Fetterman, are a dying breed of individuals who believe in the exchange of ideas and positions with those they all may disagree with, as exemplified by the recent dinner at the White House with President Trump and Kid Rock," Fox News contributor Joe Concha told Fox News Digital in a statement about Smith's remarks. "Unfortunately, the trend on the left is to shut down anyone through censorship or otherwise anything resembling debate."

articles.title: Menacing high school running back executes one of the most punishing kickoff blocks you will ever witness

paras.en: Another week, another absurd highlight from one of the top high school running backs in the country.
It's like clockwork at this point with David Gabriel-Georges — a Tennessee Vols commit who is currently the No. 2 RB in America. Every week, it's something new.

Way back in August, he dazzled America with a 3-touchdown showing on opening night. Not bad! In September, I featured Gabriel-Georges again, this time because he made an entire defense look like a pee-wee football team and rushed for five more touchdowns in a blowout win.
And now here we are again, in the meat of October, with another David Gabriel Georges highlight. Amazing.

For those who haven't kept up, I've taken it upon myself here at OutKick to highlight at least one high school football play/ player/ story each and every Saturday during the season. These guys are all about to be millionaires with the silly NIL rules, so we might as well get ahead of the curve and start identifying them early.
So far this season, we've seen a wild Hail Mary in Florida, an entire California team get suspended because the mascot shot the bird to some fans, and a giant running back in Kentucky smashing heads.
Today, we're going BACK to where this all began, and checking in with the best running back in America laying the WOOD on special teams:
Whoaaaaaaaaaa Nellie! Lordy. What a hit. That probably gets you ejected in the NFL nowadays. But not in high school football, baby! It's the Wild Wild West down there, which is why it's the best.
LOOK at that block! That would make Troy Polamalu wince. Just a punishing hit from a punishing running back.
And for those concerned that the senior Tennessee commit was expending too much energy on special teams to be an effective running back ... rest easy tonight.
He absolutely manhandled the poor fellas over at Ensworth last night to the tune of 139 yards and two scores.

articles.title: Death toll rises to 9 in church attack as officials blame 'extremist' Islamist ideology

paras.en: A group of gunmen stormed a Christian church in Jordan during a funeral on Friday, killing nine people and injuring more than two dozen, according to authorities.
The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 55 miles south of the capital, Amman.
Jordanian Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said Saturday that one critically injured patient remained hospitalized at Prince Ali Military Hospital in unstable condition.
Karak is home to a sizable Christian minority, and Momani sought to emphasize that Christians are "part of Jordan's national fabric."
It remains unclear whether the gunmen were affiliated with any terror group, and Jordanian authorities have not announced any arrests in connection with the attack.
Footage shown on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen armed with what appeared to be pistols approaching the church and opening fire, The Associated Press reported.
A third man carrying what appeared to be a semiautomatic rifle joined them moments later, before all three rushed toward the church.
Photos and videos from witnesses show broken glass and pools of blood inside the church. After the location was secured by police, two bodies covered with blankets were seen outside the church.
Dorgham Halasa told the AP that intense gunfire erupted in the church some 15 minutes after the funeral service began. People began running, he said.
Halasa said he didn't see the gunmen, but said others he spoke with reported seeing at least four of them. Jordanian authorities had not confirmed the number of attackers as of Saturday.
On Friday, King Abdullah II said Jordan will "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties."

"Whoever imagines that the bullets of treachery can divide the ranks of Jordanians will fail in his endeavor before our steadfastness and unity," he added. "Our deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded."
Jordan announced three days of national mourning following the attack, according to the state-run Petra News Agency.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Suspect arrested over fire at Hitler’s ‘Eagle’s Nest’ retreat in Bavaria
articles.author: Donna Ferguson and agencies

paras.en: Police have arrested a 33-year-old German citizen after a fire ripped through Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat in Bavaria, leaving the historic Nazi meeting place – known as the Eagle’s Nest – largely destroyed.

About 200 firefighters were deployed on Friday night to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator’s remote, purpose-built Kehlsteinhaus residence, a protected building on the peak of Obersalzberg in southern Germany.
Flames rose high into the air as firefighters approached the scene to find the building “completely ablaze”, police said, adding that nobody was injured in the fire.
Lisa Maier, a police spokesperson, said firefighters struggled to tackle the blaze due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres (6,000ft).
The building, which was one of the few undamaged monuments of the Hitler era, was only accessible with “heavy breathing apparatus”, she said.
Built by the Nazis and formally inaugurated by Hitler on his birthday in 1939, the Eagle’s Nest has been preserved as a monument to “the insanity of the regime”, according to its website.

The building is only accessible via a road cut into the mountain through previously impassable terrain. Nazis would enter a tunnel and take a 124-metre brass lift buried in the mountain to get inside the building.

Authorities were alerted to the fire when a smoke detector triggered a fire alarm at about 9.15pm, police said. When firefighters arrived on the scene at about 9.50pm, the entire building was engulfed in flames.
Fire departments from six municipalities sent emergency personnel to tackle the blaze and the Bavarian Red Cross, the local mountain rescue service and the police also attended.
No reason for the fire was given, but German media reported that investigators suspected it was the result of arson. Firefighters found no one inside the building.
Efforts to fight the fire were hampered by a strong wind and rain, which turned into the year’s first snow, and firefighters had to pull out overnight after several hours.
The blaze was reportedly still burning at 7am on Saturday but appeared to be out later in the morning, although smoke continued to rise from the building.

A police spokesperson told the German tabloid Bild: “It is damaged to a large extent. The house is unlikely to be saved.” Officers blocked access to the road leading to the retreat, according to an Agence France-Presse photographer.
Maier said police were still investigating and would hold a news conference later on Saturday.

The 33-year-old suspect arrested by the police was a German citizen who had ties to the area but did not live there. Prosecutors said he showed signs of mental illness and after being questioned he was being sent to a psychiatric facility.
The possibility of a political motive for the blaze would be investigated, but police said there was nothing to indicate anyone else was involved.

The Eagle’s Nest was constructed between 1937 and 1938 and forms part of the toxic legacy of Hitler’s Third Reich, which was responsible for the deaths of millions of Jews as well as Roma, LGBTQ people and communists in the Holocaust.
It became legendary in the postwar period and was often depicted as an essential meeting place in US war films, although in reality Hitler rarely visited the complex.
Since 1952 the building has housed an exhibition by the Institute for Contemporary History recounting its Nazi history, and a restaurant.
Officials indicated that the building, which is owned by Bavaria’s state government, would be restored after discussions with local officials, historians and conservators.
“We’re not going to leave a ruin there,” Joachim Herrmann, Bavaria’s interior minister, told reporters, adding that it was important to continue to do “the work of remembrance”.
Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Thousands march in Paris and other French cities as protests take place across Europe – Europe live
articles.author: Marina Dunbar (now); Frances Mao and Emily Mackay (earlier)

paras.en: Demonstrations kick off across France's major cities amid heavy security
paras.zh: 在严密的安全措施下，法国主要城市的示威活动开始

paras.en: People have also begun marching in the port city of Marseille, France’s second-most populous city. Thousands had gathered for the procession down the Canabière main street.
paras.zh: 人们也开始在法国人口第二多的港口城市马赛游行。成千上万的人聚集在Canabière大街上游行。

paras.en: In Lyon, crowds have set off from Place Jean-Macé, chanting slogans and singing, flanked by rows of police officers. Crowds are also marching in Toulouse and Lille.
paras.zh: 在里昂，人群从让-马塞广场出发，高呼口号和唱歌，两侧是一排排的警察。人群也在图卢兹和里尔游行。

paras.en: Meanwhile protest restrictions remain in place in other cities, where last-minute legal appeals have failed.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在其他城市，抗议限制仍然存在，最后一刻的法律上诉已经失败。

paras.en: In Bordeaux, demonstrators have shown up at the Place de la Bourse despite a city-wide ban and tram cancellations.
paras.zh: 在波尔多，尽管全市禁令和电车取消，但示威者仍出现在交易所广场。

paras.en: “Whether the protest is banned or not, we will support the high school students’ movement and we won’t abandon them. We are parents, we were young once, and we are also workers,” said Brigitte Couderc, general secretary of the CGT-Commerce and Services union in the Gironde region told Le Monde.
paras.zh: “无论抗议活动是否被禁止，我们都会支持高中生运动，我们不会放弃他们。我们是父母，我们曾经年轻，我们也是工人，”吉伦特地区CGT商业和服务工会秘书长Brigitte Couderc告诉Le Monde。

paras.en: In Nice, police said they had ordered the dispersal of a crowd of several hundred people who had gathered at Place Masséna despite all gatherings being banned.
paras.zh: 在尼斯，警方表示，尽管所有集会都被禁止，但他们已下令驱散聚集在马塞纳广场的数百人。

paras.en: France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, earlier said that there was a turnout of about 35,000 people in marches across the country, compared with 60,000 last Saturday. He said authorities had counted 136 public street actions, down from 264 the previous weekend.
paras.zh: 法国内政部长洛朗·努涅斯（ Laurent Nuñez ）早些时候表示，全国各地的游行人数约为3.5万人，而上周六为6万人。他说，当局统计了136起公共街头行动，低于上周末的264起。

paras.en: Meanwhile in Albania, more than 2000 police have been deployed around Tirana on the 12th day of student-led protests amid reports of concerted efforts to stop demonstrators entering the capital.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在阿尔巴尼亚，在学生领导的抗议活动的第12天，地拉那周围部署了2000多名警察，据报道，他们共同努力阻止示威者进入首都。

paras.en: Protests initially spurred by fury over a planned Trump family-backed resort in Albania have turned increasingly violent as students have joined what growing numbers are now calling a revolution to oust prime minister Edi Rama. Today, rally numbers swelled with demonstrators traveling to Tirana from cities across the Balkan state and as teachers, doctors and labour unions also weighed in.
paras.zh: 最初因特朗普家族支持的阿尔巴尼亚度假村计划而引发的抗议活动变得越来越暴力，因为学生们加入了越来越多的人现在称之为推翻总理埃迪·拉马的革命。今天，集会人数激增，示威者从巴尔干半岛各地的城市前往地拉那，教师、医生和工会也参与其中。

paras.en: But police also stand increasingly accused of heavy-handed tactics amid reports of civilians being plucked from the streets by masked officers and riot police increasingly resorting to using rubber bullets, batons, tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds.
paras.zh: 但随着有报道称蒙面警察和防暴警察越来越多地使用橡皮子弹、警棍、催泪瓦斯和水炮驱散人群，警察也越来越多地被指控采用高压战术。

paras.en: Speaking to the Guardian after spending several hours at Tirana’s National Trauma hospital earlier in the day, Kei Brisku, who heads the Abania Rehabilitation Centre for Trauma and Torture, said there were growing concerns about “the mass and random use” of rubber bullets.
paras.zh: 阿巴尼亚创伤和酷刑康复中心负责人Kei Brisku当天早些时候在地拉那国家创伤医院呆了几个小时后对《卫报》说，人们越来越担心橡皮子弹的“大规模和随意使用”。

paras.en: “Nine protestors, five women and four men, were badly wounded by rubber bullets today and are now in hospital,” he said.
paras.zh: 他说： “9名抗议者，包括5名妇女和4名男子，今天被橡皮子弹重伤，现在正在医院接受治疗。”

paras.en: “The use of rubber bullets against violent protesters may be justified under applicable regulations ... however, their indiscriminate use against crowds is unacceptable, as it risks harming peaceful protesters and bystanders who pose no threat.”
paras.zh: “根据适用的法规，对暴力抗议者使用橡皮子弹可能是合理的……然而，对人群滥用橡皮子弹是不可接受的，因为它有可能伤害不构成威胁的和平抗议者和旁观者。”

paras.en: In power for 13 years, Rama has resolutely refused to resign. While he has offered to discuss the “ legitimate concerns” of students, he has ruled out talking with hooligans who resort to violence.
paras.zh: 拉玛执政13年，坚决拒绝辞职。虽然他提出要讨论学生的“合理担忧” ，但他排除了与诉诸暴力的流氓交谈的可能性。

paras.en: Last week, the socialist leader told the Guardian the “violence in Tirana is very real,” as he dismissed accusations that his government was employing underhand tactics to fast-track the controversial resort championed by Jared Kushner, the US president’s son-in-law.
paras.zh: 上周，这位社会主义领导人告诉《卫报》， “地拉那的暴力事件非常真实” ，因为他驳斥了有关他的政府正在采用秘密策略来快速追踪美国总统女婿贾里德·库什纳（ Jared Kushner ）所倡导的有争议的度假村的指控。

paras.en: The NFL (American football league) closed its “NFL House” in Paris as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.
paras.zh: NFL （美式橄榄球联盟）关闭了位于巴黎的“NFL之家” ，因为这座城市为街头抗议做好了准备，警察大量存在，店面被封锁。

paras.en: The league announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning through its “OnePass” app, according to the AP, citing “potential accessibility issues.”
paras.zh: 据美联社报道，该联盟周六早上通过其“OnePass”应用程序向粉丝宣布关闭，理由是“潜在的无障碍问题”。

paras.en: Security concerns have overshadowed the NFL’s planned debut in Paris. The New Orleans Saints will play the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday at Stade de France in the league’s first-ever regular-season game in France.
paras.zh: 安全问题给NFL计划在巴黎的首次亮相蒙上了阴影。新奥尔良圣徒队将于周日在法兰西体育场与匹兹堡钢人队比赛，这是该联盟在法国的首场常规赛。

paras.en: Major museums including the Louvre and Orsay Museum are also closed Saturday, though tourists were seen lined up to enter Notre Dame Cathedral.
paras.zh: 包括卢浮宫和奥赛博物馆在内的主要博物馆也在周六关闭，但游客们排队进入巴黎圣母院。

paras.en: 25,000 people rally in Madrid for pension guarantees
paras.zh: 25,000人在马德里集会争取养老金保障

paras.en: Spanish authorities say about 25,000 demonstrators have marched through the country’s capital demanding protections to the state pension scheme.
paras.zh: 西班牙当局表示，约有25,000名示威者在该国首都游行，要求保护国家养老金计划。

paras.en: Spain is voting in a snap parliamentary election in a few weeks and this has been a key topic of concern. Spain’s Socalist prime minister Pedro Sanchez, who called the snap election after struggling to get pension reforms through parliament, has accused conservative parties of holding back inflation-linked increases.
paras.zh: 西班牙将在几周内举行议会选举，这是一个令人担忧的关键话题。西班牙社会党总理佩德罗·桑切斯（ Pedro Sanchez ）在努力通过议会进行养老金改革后宣布提前选举，他指责保守党派阻碍与通货膨胀相关的增长。

paras.en: Protesters marched from the Atocha train station to the Gran Via shopping avenue in the Spanish capital.
paras.zh: 抗议者从Atocha火车站游行到西班牙首都的Gran Via购物大道。

paras.en: Some expressed concern about portions of their state pensions being privatised in the future. About 6.8 million Spaniards receive a state pension and fiscally conservative, right-wing politicians have raised questions over how sustainable the current system is.
paras.zh: 一些人对未来部分国家养老金被私有化表示担忧。大约680万西班牙人领取国家养老金，财政上保守的右翼政客对现行制度的可持续性提出了质疑。

paras.en: Spain has also seem major protests in recent months over increasingly unaffordable housing and renters’ rights.
paras.zh: 近几个月来，西班牙似乎也就越来越难以负担的住房和租房者权利举行了重大抗议活动。

paras.en: Are French high school buildings dilapidated and rat-infested with collapsing ceilings?
paras.zh: 法国高中建筑物是否破旧不堪，天花板是否会倒塌？

paras.en: Some are, namely in certain cities and low-income suburbs. Videos filmed by students and teachers have shown leaks, scurrying rats, holes in walls and ceilings, broken toilets and not enough chairs or tables, meaning teachers have to carry them from classroom to classroom. Some children said they had to learn in class while leaks were pouring into buckets, or move desks to avoid getting wet. Many school classrooms experienced temperatures over 35C (95F) in the heatwaves of last May and June.
paras.zh: 有些是，即在某些城市和低收入郊区。学生和教师拍摄的视频显示漏水、匆忙奔跑的老鼠、墙壁和天花板上的洞、破损的厕所和没有足够的椅子或桌子，这意味着教师必须将它们从教室搬到教室。一些孩子说，他们必须在课堂上学习，而漏水倒在水桶里，或者移动办公桌以避免被弄湿。去年5月和6月的热浪中，许多学校教室的温度超过35摄氏度（ 95华氏度）。

paras.en: Estimates in recent years have pointed to thousands of French schools at all levels, both primary and secondary, in need of repair. These include many 1960s school buildings. French regions are responsible for upkeep of high school buildings, but have asked for higher budgets from the government. A senate report has advised that billions need to be spent in the coming years to renovate and repair schools, as well as to address the impact of the climate crisis.
Tens of thousands of people have turned out to the heavily policed demonstrations across Franceand they have been, on the whole, quite contained so far.

Some sections of the crowd could be seen singing and dancing in Paris as they walked along the route, which was pushed to the city’s fringes at the last minute as police sought to move the march away from the fortified city centre.
In Lyon, police used teargas early on in the banned demonstration to disperse some of the crowd but people were still able to walk on.

In the last half hour there’s also a been of bit of rough activity in Marseille between police and a few dozen people. The French broadcaster BFMTV has shown live footage of masked attendees throwing bins, flares going off and spot fires in the street. There are cordons of riot police around.

Overall though, the heavy policing has appeared to be successful so far in staving off the type of looting, ransacking and violent activity we saw on the fringes of the marches last week. The government has added on 20% more officers, for a 70,000 strong force across the country.
Earlier today, the French interior minister had said protest numbers – at about 36,000 in the morning- were about half of what they were last Saturday.
At the Paris march, Nadège, a communications worker, said she was at Place de la République last Saturday when teargas hit. But that hadn’t deterred her.
I’m out again peacefully today to support everyone who is brave enough to demonstrate. It does take courage. People are afraid now.
We have to keep our rights alive. We’ve seen what happens in the US when a bad president is in power. In France, it’s our legal right to protest in the street and I’m here to defend that.
The French president had hosted student representatives for a highly anticipated meeting yesterday afternoon.
Going in, the student leaders had already expressed cynicism over whether the French president would adequately address their concerns.

Pupils in Paris began protests over the quality of their education four weeks ago – and their spirit has since inspired demonstrations elsewhere, across the nation and also into other countries, such as Italy and Greece.
French high schoolers say they’re fed up with the deteriorating state of their school buildings, overworked and underpaid teachers, and packed classrooms.

They’re demanding school renovations and upgrades, better study conditions and the scrapping of the Parcoursup univeristy admissions platform which was introduced in 2018 and has long been criticised for lack of transparency.
Macron held a two-and-a-half hours-long meeting with 20 students.

Nathanael Combary, president of campaign group High School Renewal, said the president had been “attentive” and they would continue talks with Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Monday on proposed changes like reform of Parcoursup.
But he and other student leaders called on their peers to continue protesting this weekend.
The radical-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the La France Insoumise party, is also marching in the Parisian procession.
Speaking to the press earlier he said the protests would continue every week until Emmanuel Macron and his government addressed the public’s demands.
He said Macron “is going to understand that this is going to repeat itself every week” and urged the president, “there is still time for him to concede” to the students’ wishes.
Macron met with student leaders on Friday for the first time since the demonstrations began a month ago. More on that meeting next.
Demonstrations kick off across France's major cities amid heavy security
paras.zh: 在严密的安全措施下，法国主要城市的示威活动开始

paras.en: People have also begun marching in the port city of Marseille, France’s second-most populous city. Thousands had gathered for the procession down the Canabière main street.
paras.zh: 人们也开始在法国人口第二多的港口城市马赛游行。成千上万的人聚集在Canabière大街上游行。

paras.en: In Lyon, crowds have set off from Place Jean-Macé, chanting slogans and singing, flanked by rows of police officers. Crowds are also marching in Toulouse and Lille.
paras.zh: 在里昂，人群从让-马塞广场出发，高呼口号和唱歌，两侧是一排排的警察。人群也在图卢兹和里尔游行。

paras.en: Meanwhile protest restrictions remain in place in other cities, where last-minute legal appeals have failed.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在其他城市，抗议限制仍然存在，最后一刻的法律上诉已经失败。

paras.en: In Bordeaux, demonstrators have shown up at the Place de la Bourse despite a city-wide ban and tram cancellations.
paras.zh: 在波尔多，尽管全市禁令和电车取消，但示威者仍出现在交易所广场。

paras.en: “Whether the protest is banned or not, we will support the high school students’ movement and we won’t abandon them. We are parents, we were young once, and we are also workers,” said Brigitte Couderc, general secretary of the CGT-Commerce and Services union in the Gironde region told Le Monde.
paras.zh: “无论抗议活动是否被禁止，我们都会支持高中生运动，我们不会放弃他们。我们是父母，我们曾经年轻，我们也是工人，”吉伦特地区CGT商业和服务工会秘书长Brigitte Couderc告诉Le Monde。

paras.en: In Nice, police said they had ordered the dispersal of a crowd of several hundred people who had gathered at Place Masséna despite all gatherings being banned.
paras.zh: 在尼斯，警方表示，尽管所有集会都被禁止，但他们已下令驱散聚集在马塞纳广场的数百人。

paras.en: France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, earlier said that there was a turnout of about 35,000 people in marches across the country, compared with 60,000 last Saturday. He said authorities had counted 136 public street actions, down from 264 the previous weekend.
paras.zh: 法国内政部长洛朗·努涅斯（ Laurent Nuñez ）早些时候表示，全国各地的游行人数约为3.5万人，而上周六为6万人。他说，当局统计了136起公共街头行动，低于上周末的264起。

paras.en: My colleague Angelique Chrisafis has been at Place d’Italie in the French capital.
Many cardboard signs held by demonstrators in Paris referenced the dozens of ongoing inquiries into mutilations and injuries by police weapons in the four weeks since high school protests began.

One 21-year-old student from a Paris science faculty that is currently blockaded by demonstrators, said: “We feel in France that we are increasingly living in an authoritarian regime that is trying to stop our democratic right to protest in the street.”
The thousands gathered in the French capital have begun walking along the designated 1.5km route from Porte d’Italie to Porte de Vincennes.
The metro trains headed to the 13th arrondisement starting point were packed.
The march has been organised by a coalition of unions, the CGT, CFDT, FSU, and Solidaires, supporting student federations, and there are the flags and banners of these various grooups.
But there are also protesters of all stripes – many young people, but also families, office workers, retirees.
Thousands of retired people and others also marched in the Spanish capital, Madrid, on Saturday, to demand that state pensions should be protected.

Pensions have become a key battleground ahead of next month’s snap election, with the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, arguing that the conservative opposition Popular party wants to privatise pensions.
French police make 135 arrests, interior minister says
France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, has said that police have made 135 arrests in relation to the nationwide protests, and seized a variety of weapons.

Weapons confiscated included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, Nuñez said. He added that, so far, “there has been no major incident”.
An anti-government rally is taking place in the Albanian capital, Tirana, after days of violent unrest in the city.

Protesters have been calling for the prime minister, Edi Rama, to resign since last week, and demanding action against corruption and poor living standards. More than 300 people have been injured in the protests amid clashes with police, with dozens of demonstrators detained and damage to government buildings.
“There is a lot of anger,” activist Sidorela Vatnikaj told AFP, labelling the movement a “revolution”.
“It’s not a matter of only students, it’s not a matter only of environmental struggles ... It’s a matter of the state of rights and state of law.”

AFP is reporting that police in Lyon, south-east France, fired teargas to disperse about 150 protesters near the city centre – where demonstrations had been banned – when they briefly tried to block a road.
A 21-year-old student, speaking anonymously, told AFP: “The police are really mobile ... They come and disperse marches before they even form.”
Demonstrators are on the move in Orléans, where Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party is holding its congress.

Thousands of people are marching, Agence France-Presse reports, shouting anti-fascist slogans and calling for Le Pen to be imprisoned, and for the French president, Emmanuel Macron, to resign. Police put the number of marchers at 11,000, while organisers said 26,000 took part.
The Guardian’s Paris correspondent, Angelique Chrisafis, has been speaking with more demonstrators in the French capital.
Pierre, 60, a retired banking consultant, said he was demonstrating to support young people’s demands for improvements in education.

I think young people need to take part in building the future they will live in. I have an eight-year-old granddaughter, I want her to have a brighter future than the sombre times we are facing today. There is a complete refusal by the government to listen to people’s demands and feelings.
Emma, 35, a science podcaster, was protesting for the second Saturday.

I want to be part of a mass of people standing up for the schoolchildren protesters and saying the misery of the few is the concern of us all. I feel anger and despair at the rise of fascism and misery in the world and I want people to unite to campaign for something better.
Further student and youth demonstrations across the political spectrum are expected in Italian cities today after major anti-government protests kicked off last weekend.
Like in France, several of those demonstrations at times spiralled into looting and clashes with police.
Prime Minister Georgia Meloni – deeply unpopular with many young people – has deployed 500 extra soldiers to Milan and announced harsher penalties for minors, after major looting there last week.
Police said the ransacking in Milan had involved about 2,000 youths. Police have stepped up ID checks at railway stations and deployed surveillance drones.
In Rome, authorities have also stepped up patrols and shut down luxury shopping strips and are restricting access around the Circus Maximus and Piazza del Popolo.

Right-wing students have been staging a demonstration this morning, in response to largely left-wing protests held last week which railed against Meloni’s government and called for better schools, affordable housing and cost-of-living measures.
An anti-war protest is also scheduled in a few hours time at Piazza della Repubblica.

articles.title: Ukraine’s military says Starlink satellite connection stable after recent restrictions
articles.author: Donna Ferguson

paras.en: Ukraine’s military has a “stable connection to Starlink”, the Ukrainian government has said, 10 days after its ability to use the satellite communications system was suddenly restricted.
paras.zh: 乌克兰政府表示，乌克兰军方在使用卫星通信系统的能力突然受到限制10天后， “与Starlink建立了稳定的联系”。

paras.en: The Starlink satellite terminals, which are produced by Elon Musk’s SpaceX but managed by the US government, are a key component of Ukraine’s military operations. Sudden speed restrictions on the terminals, which capped operations at speeds of 160km/h (99mph), led to the failure of several Ukrainian combat missions earlier this month.
paras.zh: Starlink卫星终端由埃隆·马斯克（ Elon Musk ）的SpaceX公司生产，但由美国政府管理，是乌克兰军事行动的关键组成部分。码头的突然速度限制限制了160公里/小时（ 99英里/小时）的速度，导致本月早些时候几次乌克兰作战任务失败。

paras.en: The military’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones was hampered and some Ukrainian operations to strike behind enemy frontlines were cancelled. Russia was able to launch ballistic missiles at Ukraine without any advance warning from the US.
paras.zh: 军方拦截俄罗斯攻击无人机的能力受到阻碍，乌克兰在敌方前线后方的一些打击行动被取消。俄罗斯能够在没有美国事先警告的情况下向乌克兰发射弹道导弹。

paras.en: The speed restrictions coincided with the announcement by Donald Trump of a US deal to buy Russian diesel, although the US president initially denied that his administration was behind the decision to cut intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
paras.zh: 速度限制恰逢唐纳德特朗普宣布美国购买俄罗斯柴油的交易，尽管美国总统最初否认他的政府是决定削减与乌克兰的情报共享的幕后黑手。

paras.en: “I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” Trump said, referring to Musk, SpaceX’s chief executive.
paras.zh: “我不知道是不是任何人，但不是我，也不认为是伊隆，”特朗普在谈到SpaceX首席执行官马斯克时说。

paras.en: However, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, appeared to throw suspicion on Musk when he defended Trump last Wednesday. “The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk,” Rubio said. “That’s a private company. The president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything.”
paras.zh: 然而，美国国务卿马可·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)上周三为特朗普辩护时，似乎对马斯克表示怀疑。“总统与Starlink和Starshield以及马斯克先生做出的决定无关，”卢比奥说。“那是一家私营公司。总裁不经营那家公司，也不能指示那家公司做任何事情。”

paras.en: Musk was quick to blame the limits on Starshield on the Trump administration, writing on X last week that the systems were “owned and controlled by the US government”. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately Potus [president of the United States],” he wrote.
paras.zh: 马斯克很快将Starshield的限制归咎于特朗普政府，上周在X上写道，这些系统“由美国政府拥有和控制”。他写道： “对速度或使用的任何限制都由美国军方决定，最终由波图斯（美国总统）决定。”

paras.en: The US vice-president, JD Vance, backed Musk on Thursday, saying the billionaire “doesn’t want to get in the middle of what is a war between two state actors without the United States government effectively directing him on what to do”.
paras.zh: 美国副总统万斯(JD Vance)周四支持马斯克，称这位亿万富翁“不想介入两国之间的战争，除非美国政府有效地指导他该怎么做”。

paras.en: Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, blamed both parties: “It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed … And technically, SpaceX did it.”
paras.zh: 乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基（ Volodymyr Zelenskyy ）指责双方： “这是美国政府限制速度的信息……从技术上讲， SpaceX做到了。”

paras.en: There were no similar restrictions on Starshield terminals in EU countries and that they applied only to Ukraine, he added. “In other words, this is a planned operation.”
paras.zh: 他补充说，欧盟国家的Starshield终端没有类似的限制，它们仅适用于乌克兰。“换句话说，这是一项有计划的行动。”

paras.en: He said the decision would “bring a lot of human losses … of course people would die”.
paras.zh: 他说，这一决定将“带来很多人命损失……当然会有人死亡”。

paras.en: Announcing the restoration of the system on Saturday in a diplomatic video address on the Telegram app, Zelenskyy expressed his gratitude to his US allies, including Trump and the US state department, for resolving the operational issue: “The most important development for today is that Starlink and Starshield have resumed operations at their pre-restriction speeds. The speeds are now at the level we need.”
paras.zh: Zelenskyy周六在Telegram应用程序上的外交视频演讲中宣布恢复该系统，他对包括特朗普和美国国务院在内的美国盟友解决运营问题表示感谢： “今天最重要的发展是Starlink和Starshield以其预限制速度恢复运营。现在的速度已经达到我们需要的水平。”

paras.en: The restoration began overnight. “By this morning, the speeds were already sufficient for operational use,” Zelenskyy said. “This is very important and significant for our frontline logistics and for defending Ukraine against jet-powered Shaheds.”
paras.zh: 修复工作一夜之间开始。Zelenskyy说： “到今天早上，速度已经足够用于操作。” “这对我们的前线物流以及保卫乌克兰免受喷气式飞机驱动的Shaheds非常重要。”

paras.en: On Thursday, Trump had claimed the service was running again at full speed, but a European official speaking to the Associated Press denied the service was fully functioning.
paras.zh: 周四，特朗普声称该服务再次全速运行，但一名欧洲官员在接受美联社采访时否认该服务完全正常运行。

paras.en: When asked by reporters whether he would tell Musk to stop “messing around” with Ukraine’s access to Starlink on Friday, the US president said: “I’ve not spoken to him. I might have to … I’ve heard it was fixed. But if it’s not, I’ll speak to him … If there is a problem, I’ll get it straightened out.”
paras.zh: 当记者问及他是否会告诉马斯克周五停止“胡闹”乌克兰进入Starlink时，这位美国总统说： “我没有和他说过话。我可能不得不……我听说它已经修好了。但如果没有，我会和他谈谈……如果有问题，我会把它弄清楚的。”

paras.en: He then described Musk as a “very brilliant” and “very good” person.
paras.zh: 然后，他形容马斯克是一个“非常聪明”和“非常好”的人。

articles.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits

paras.en: Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network.
paras.zh: 乌克兰国防部长表示，在军方在卫星互联网连接受到限制数天之后，乌克兰现在与Starlink建立了“稳定的连接”。

paras.en: Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.
paras.zh: 基辅依靠Starlink及其军用级同行Starshield来驾驶无人机并在乌克兰境内开展业务，但上周指责美国总统唐纳德·特朗普告诉所有者埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)对其进行限制。

paras.en: This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".
paras.zh: 这意味着无人机在以161公里/小时（ 100英里/小时）或更高速度行驶时会失去连接。特朗普否认这样做，然后说马斯克已经“放回去”。

paras.en: Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.
paras.zh: 国防部长Yevhenii Khmara表示，现在可以在网络上实现超过400公里/小时的速度，这表明已经恢复了全部能力。

paras.en: "This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.
paras.zh: 他在周六的一份声明中说： “这一结果对我们的前线，对我们的士兵，对无人机的操作，对后勤和通讯都至关重要。”

paras.en: Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.
paras.zh: 乌克兰军方广泛使用由10,000颗低地球轨道卫星组成的网络进行军事行动，特别是在战场上的偏远地区。

paras.en: Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.
paras.zh: 乌克兰同时使用民用服务Starlink和更安全的Starshield ，马斯克表示，当他暗示五角大楼可能是近期问题的幕后黑手时，它由美国军方控制。

paras.en: Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯无权使用Starlink ，因此当乌克兰派遣远程导弹或无人机深入俄罗斯打击炼油厂时，该网络不起作用。

paras.en: The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
paras.zh: Starlink的崩溃始于上周，发生在特朗普与乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基（ Volodymyr Zelensky ）就乌克兰对俄罗斯石油基础设施的罢工进行更广泛的外交争执期间。

paras.en: Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.
paras.zh: 面对下个月的中期选举，特朗普放弃了对俄罗斯的一些制裁，并同意为美国市场进口俄罗斯柴油，此举受到乌克兰及其欧洲盟友的批评。

paras.en: Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, have pushed global prices higher.
paras.zh: 特朗普表示，对俄罗斯炼油厂的打击已经推高了全球油价，而基辅表示，这些炼油厂对于阻止莫斯科战争努力的主要收入来源至关重要。

paras.en: While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war.
paras.zh: 虽然袭击对全球燃料价格产生了影响，但今年的上涨主要是由于伊朗战争。

paras.en: Zelensky said that, as well as seemingly limiting Starlink capability in Ukraine, the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump also denied.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基表示，除了似乎限制了Starlink在乌克兰的能力外，美国还威胁说，如果罢工不停止，美国将撤回情报共享，特朗普也否认了这一点。

paras.en: Meanwhile, fighting on the ground continues.
paras.zh: 与此同时，地面上的战斗仍在继续。

paras.en: Russia's ministry of defence wrote on Telegram on Saturday that their air defences shot down 616 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones, striking a number of regions across the country, including Russian-annexed Crimea.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯国防部周六在Telegram上写道，他们的防空部队击落了616架乌克兰固定翼无人机，袭击了全国多个地区，包括俄罗斯吞并的克里米亚。

paras.en: Sergey Aksyonov, the region's Moscow-backed governor, said restrictions on electricity and water had been put in place because of power cuts caused by the drone strike.
paras.zh: 该地区由莫斯科支持的州长谢尔盖·阿克肖诺夫（ Sergey Aksyonov ）表示，由于无人机袭击造成的停电，对电力和水的限制已经到位。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Ukrainian authorities said they struck a missile component manufacturer, a chemical plant and an aircraft at a military airfield inside Russia in the past 24 hours.
paras.zh: 与此同时，乌克兰当局表示，他们在过去24小时内在俄罗斯境内的一个军用机场袭击了一家导弹部件制造商、一家化工厂和一架飞机。

paras.en: They also said that Russia carried out 88 air strikes using 309 glide bombs and 10,270 kamikaze drones on Friday.
paras.zh: 他们还表示，俄罗斯周五使用309枚滑翔炸弹和10,270架神风无人机进行了88次空袭。

articles.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after revealing diagnosis

paras.en: Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year.
paras.zh: 小唐纳德·特朗普（ Donald Trump Jr ）的前妻瓦妮莎·特朗普（ Vanessa Trump ）宣布，她在今年早些时候被诊断出患有乳腺癌后

paras.en: Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free".
paras.zh: 现年48岁的特朗普与唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)总统的长子有五个孩子，她在她19岁的女儿凯(Kai)的Instagram账户上分享了一个简短的视频，称她最近的测试结果“很清楚，所以我终于没有癌症了”。

paras.en: The video, posted on Friday, teases the release of a longer YouTube video to come on Saturday, in which Vanessa and Kai Trump will discuss breast cancer awareness and prevention, Kai wrote in the caption.
paras.zh: Kai在标题中写道，周五发布的这段视频嘲笑了周六发布的一段更长的YouTube视频，其中Vanessa和Kai Trump将讨论乳腺癌的认识和预防。

paras.en: Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods.
paras.zh: 瓦妮莎·特朗普（ Vanessa Trump ）于2018年与小特朗普分手，并于去年宣布她已开始与美国职业高尔夫球手泰格·伍兹（ Tiger

paras.en: "October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram.
paras.zh: Kai Trump在Instagram上写道： “10月是乳腺癌宣传月，是提高对早期发现、教育和支持乳腺癌患者的认识的时候。”

paras.en: "I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued.
paras.zh: 她继续说道： “我和妈妈以及Nicole Saphier医生坐下来谈论我妈妈患乳腺癌的旅程，并了解更多关于预防和早期发现的信息。”

paras.en: Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben.
paras.zh: Kai的帖子收到了超过20,000个赞和数百条评论，来自提供支持和祝福的人，包括美国歌手和媒体名人Mary Millben。

paras.en: In Friday's video, Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team.
paras.zh: 在周五的视频中，特朗普说她在4月份首次被诊断出患有乳腺癌。她在5月份公开宣布了这一诊断，并在社交媒体帖子中表示，她已经接受了手术，并正在与她的医疗团队制定治疗计划。

paras.en: According to the American Cancer Society, the average risk of a woman in the US developing breast cancer is about 1 in 8, or 13%. The disease also accounts for 30% of all new female cancers every year, according to the group.
paras.zh: 根据美国癌症协会的数据，美国女性患乳腺癌的平均风险约为1/8 ，即13%。据该组织称，这种疾病每年还占所有新发女性癌症的30%。

paras.en: Surgery cures most breast cancers, but if some disease remains, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and endocrine therapy can reduce the long-term risk.
paras.zh: 手术可以治愈大多数乳腺癌，但如果一些疾病仍然存在，化疗、放疗和内分泌治疗可以降低长期风险。

paras.en: Treatments have been advancing, including more targeted therapies for early breast cancer, new types of hormonal therapies, and more precise and effective radiotherapy.
paras.zh: 治疗方法一直在进步，包括更有针对性的早期乳腺癌治疗、新型激素治疗以及更精确有效的放射治疗。

articles.title: Watch as fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat

paras.en: Watch as fire engulfs Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
paras.zh: 观看火焰吞噬希特勒山顶的鹰巢度假胜地

paras.en: Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, known as the Eagle's Nest, was engulfed in flames on Friday night while police arrested a 33-year-old male suspect.
paras.zh: 阿道夫·希特勒（ Adolf Hitler ）的阿尔卑斯山度假胜地被称为鹰巢（ Eagle's Nest ） ，周五晚上被火焰吞没，警方逮捕了一名33岁的男性嫌疑人。

paras.en: The residence, called the Kehlsteinhaus, is above the town of Berchtesgaden. It was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.
paras.zh: 这座名为凯尔施泰因豪斯（ Kehlsteinhaus ）的住宅位于贝希特斯加登（ Berchtesgaden ）镇上方。它是第二次世界大战期间纳粹独裁者及其随从在该地区使用的几座建筑物之一。

paras.en: Hitler also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.
paras.zh: 希特勒还将该地区作为宣传电影的背景，将他描绘成动物和自然的爱好者。

paras.en: Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed", with the public urged to avoid the area.
paras.zh: 当地媒体报道说，该遗址“基本上被摧毁” ，公众敦促避开该地区。

articles.title: Carlisle Launches EL121 Disc Brakes for Improved Performance and Wear Life

paras.en: Carlisle Launches EL121 Disc Brakes for Improved Performance and Wear Life
paras.zh: Carlisle 推出 EL121 盘式制动器，以提高性能和磨损寿命

paras.en: (MEDINA, OH, September 12, 2023) – Carlisle Brake & Friction is excited to announce the launch of EL121 Disc Brake Pads for mine haul truck applications. The new product series will be named Extended Life, or the EL Series, and EL121 will be the first friction formulation of the series to launch.
paras.zh: （俄亥俄州梅迪纳，2023 年 9 月 12 日）——Carlisle Brake & Friction 很高兴地宣布推出适用于矿用卡车应用的 EL121 盘式制动片。新产品系列将被命名为Extended Life，或EL系列，EL121将是该系列中首款推出的摩擦配方。

paras.en: Carlisle’s EL121 Series friction material nearly doubles the service life of front-axle, mine haul truck brake pads. The result is increased equipment uptime, and reduced maintenance costs when utilizing the OEM calipers and rotors.
paras.zh: 卡莱尔的 EL121 系列摩擦材料使前轴、矿用运输卡车刹车片的使用寿命几乎延长了一倍。使用 OEM 卡钳和转子时，可以增加设备的正常运行时间并降低维护成本。

paras.en: Autonomous haul trucks experience higher pad temperatures, which drive elevated pad wear from increased braking cycles as the retarder and the service brake are applied. EL121 features a highly wear-resistant friction material blend that provides extended brake pad life with consistent and fade-resistant braking performance. EL121 is the ideal solution for today’s autonomous mine haul trucks (may also be used in manned mine haul trucks for increased performance and longevity).
paras.zh: 自动运输卡车的刹车片温度较高，当使用缓速器和行车制动器时，制动周期的增加会导致刹车片磨损加剧。 EL121 采用高度耐磨的摩擦材料混合物，可延长刹车片的使用寿命，并具有一致且防褪色的制动性能。 EL121 是当今自动矿用运输卡车的理想解决方案（也可用于载人矿用运输卡车，以提高性能和使用寿命）。

paras.en: “We understand that mine operators need to keep their haul trucks on the job and not in the shop for brake service. Our latest innovation allows for up to double the service life of the front-axle mine haul truck brake pads and are a will-fit replacement to existing OEM pads. These were thoroughly lab tested as well as field tested on Komatsu 830E-1 trucks,” said Ron Ratell, Product Line Director Friction Products at Carlisle Brake & Friction.
paras.zh: 卡莱尔制动与摩擦公司摩擦产品产品线总监 Ron Ratell 表示：“我们了解矿山运营商需要让运输卡车继续工作，而不是在车间进行制动维修。我们的最新创新技术可将前轴矿用运输卡车制动片的使用寿命延长一倍，并且是现有 OEM 制动片的理想替代品。这些制动片经过了彻底的实验室测试以及小松 830E-1 卡车的现场测试。”

paras.en: EL121 friction has been dyno tested to replicate the application and is proven to deliver an innovative, high-energy material to meet market needs. EL121 disc brake pads also feature an industry-proven mechanical retention system with backing plate technology designed for superior bonding and durability, capable of withstanding abusive conditions in even the harshest Off-Highway environments.
paras.zh: EL121 摩擦力经过测功机测试以复制应用，并被证明可以提供创新的高能材料来满足市场需求。 EL121 盘式刹车片还采用经过行业验证的机械固定系统，采用背板技术，旨在实现卓越的粘合性和耐用性，甚至能够承受最恶劣的非公路环境中的恶劣条件。

paras.en: Carlisle’s EL121 Series disc brake pads are available now through authorized Carlisle dealers and distributors. To learn more, visit https://www.carlislecbf.com/products/brake-friction/disc-brake-pads/off-highway-disc-brake-pads/el. To locate an authorized Carlisle dealer near you, search our online distributor listing https://www.carlislecbf.com/support/find-a-distributor.
paras.zh: Carlisle 的 EL121 系列盘式刹车片现已通过 Carlisle 授权经销商和分销商发售。要了解更多信息，请访问 https://www.carlislecbf.com/products/brake-friction/disc-brake-pads/off-highway-disc-brake-pads/el。要查找您附近的卡莱尔授权经销商，请搜索我们的在线经销商列表 https://www.carlislecbf.com/support/find-a-distributor。

paras.en: Carlisle Brake & Friction is a globally recognized leader in the development and manufacture of highly innovative brake and friction system solutions to service a diverse range of motion control applications. The comprehensive nature of Carlisle’s brake system expertise includes hydraulic control products, industrial brake assemblies, wet and dry friction material for brake, clutch, and transmission applications as well as aftermarket replacement products. Our full-system product offering, supported by our industry-experience staff of experts, provides our customers with brake system solutions that set them apart from their competition. www.carlislecbf.com
paras.zh: Carlisle Brake & Friction 是全球公认的高度创新制动和摩擦系统解决方案开发和制造领域的领导者，为各种运动控制应用提供服务。卡莱尔制动系统专业知识的综合性包括液压控制产品、工业制动组件、用于制动、离合器和变速箱应用的湿式和干式摩擦材料以及售后替换产品。我们的全系统产品由具有行业经验的专家团队提供支持，为我们的客户提供制动系统解决方案，使他们在竞争中脱颖而出。 www.carlislecbf.com

articles.title: Carlisle Releases Video Highlighting Solutions for Ag

paras.en: Carlisle Releases Video Highlighting Solutions for Ag
paras.zh: Carlisle 发布 Ag 视频突出显示解决方案

paras.en: Carlisle Brake & Friction launches a new product solutions video: Carlisle Solutions for Tractor Applications, to showcase all of the latest motion control technologies available for agriculture equipment, specifically tractor applications.
paras.zh: 卡莱尔制动与摩擦公司推出了新产品解决方案视频：卡莱尔拖拉机应用解决方案，展示适用于农业设备（特别是拖拉机应用）的所有最新运动控制技术。

paras.en: From power valves, to disc brakes, to PTO and shuttle clutch friction options, this video breaks down all of the features and benefits of Carlisle’s newest brake system and powertrain solutions.
paras.zh: 从动力阀到盘式制动器，再到取力器和梭式离合器摩擦选项，该视频详细介绍了卡莱尔最新制动系统和动力总成解决方案的所有功能和优点。

paras.en: For improved visualization, the video features 3D animation and demonstrations of the product fitments within a standard tractor model.
paras.zh: 为了提高可视化效果，该视频采用 3D 动画和标准拖拉机模型中的产品配件演示。

articles.title: Carlisle Suzhou Achieves Caterpillar SER Certification

paras.en: Carlisle Suzhou Achieves Caterpillar SER Certification
paras.zh: 卡莱苏州获得卡特彼勒 SER 认证

paras.en: (MEDINA, January 25, 2024) – Carlisle Brake & Friction announced its Suzhou facility has won a Supplier Excellence Recognition (SER) Certification from Caterpillar Inc. The Caterpillar SER is a new supplier management system featuring "Certified" and "Excellent" levels. Caterpillar officially launched the program in 2022. Carlisle's Suzhou manufacturing facility achieved a "Certified" level of recognition and celebrated the achievement alongside the Caterpillar team with a ceremony at the Carlisle Suzhou plant.
paras.zh: （梅迪纳，2024 年 1 月 25 日）——卡莱尔制动与摩擦公司宣布其苏州工厂获得卡特彼勒公司颁发的供应商卓越认可 (SER) 认证。卡特彼勒 SER 是一种新的供应商管理体系，具有“认证”和“优秀”级别。卡特彼勒于 2022 年正式启动该计划。卡莱尔苏州制造工厂获得了“认证”级别的认可，并与卡特彼勒团队在卡莱尔苏州工厂举行了仪式，庆祝这一成就。

paras.en: Of 27,000 suppliers, 250 were among the selected companies awarded by Caterpillar. Carlisle, a leading global supplier of brake, clutch, and transmission friction products, is the only friction products manufacturer worldwide to win the coveted certification.
paras.zh: 在 27,000 家供应商中，有 250 家入选卡特彼勒授予的奖项。 Carlisle 是全球领先的制动器、离合器和变速箱摩擦产品供应商，也是全球唯一一家获得这一令人垂涎的认证的摩擦产品制造商。

paras.en: "We are honored to be recognized by Caterpillar as a Certified level supplier," said Doug Wagner, Global VP of Sales, Carlisle Brake & Friction. "This award recognizes the superior efforts and dedication of the entire Suzhou team that supports our global business."
paras.zh: “我们很荣幸被 Caterpillar 认可为认证级供应商，”Carlisle 制动与摩擦部全球销售副总裁 Doug Wagner 说道。 “该奖项是对支持我们全球业务的整个苏州团队的卓越努力和奉献精神的认可。”

paras.en: Carlisle earned SER Certification in recognition of the company's exemplary commitment to supporting Caterpillar's global growth strategy goals.
paras.zh: Carlisle 获得了 SER 认证，以表彰该公司对支持 Caterpillar 全球增长战略目标的模范承诺。

paras.en: Carlisle Brake & Friction is a globally recognized leader in the development and manufacture of highly innovative brake and friction system solutions to service a diverse range of motion control applications. The comprehensive nature of Carlisle’s brake system expertise includes hydraulic control products, industrial brake assemblies, wet and dry friction material for brake, clutch, and transmission applications as well as aftermarket replacement products. Our full-system product offering, supported by our industry-experience staff of experts, provides our customers with brake system solutions that set them apart from their competition. www.carlislecbf.com
paras.zh: Carlisle Brake & Friction 是全球公认的高度创新制动和摩擦系统解决方案开发和制造领域的领导者，为各种运动控制应用提供服务。卡莱尔制动系统专业知识的综合性包括液压控制产品、工业制动组件、用于制动、离合器和变速箱应用的湿式和干式摩擦材料以及售后替换产品。我们的全系统产品由具有行业经验的专家团队提供支持，为我们的客户提供制动系统解决方案，使他们在竞争中脱颖而出。 www.carlislecbf.com

articles.title: Oklahoma to elect a new insurance commissioner at midterms
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: Oklahoma will elect a new insurance commissioner Nov. 3 as its current commissioner, Glen Mulready, reaches the end of his second term.
paras.zh: 俄克拉荷马州现任保险专员格伦·马尔雷迪 (Glen Mulready) 的第二任期即将结束，该州将于 11 月 3 日选出新任保险专员。

paras.en: Insurance commissioners in the state hold the position for four years and are limited to eight-years in the position.
paras.zh: 该州保险专员的任期为四年，最长为八年。

paras.en: This year’s voters will have a choice between Republican Bob Sullivan and Democrat Craig MacIntrye.
paras.zh: 今年的选民将在共和党人鲍勃·沙利文和民主党人克雷格·麦金特里之间做出选择。

paras.en: Sullivan identifies himself as a “property and casualty insurance expert” on his campaign website.
paras.zh: 沙利文在他的竞选网站上将自己称为“财产和伤亡保险专家”。

paras.en: He states his expertise includes being a certified insurance counselor, certified risk manager, chartered property and casualty underwriter, associate in Fidelity & Surety Bonding and a certified environmental specialist.
paras.zh: 他表示，他的专业知识包括成为一名经过认证的保险顾问、经过认证的风险经理、特许财产和伤亡承保人、Fidelity & Surety Bonding 助理以及经过认证的环境专家。

paras.en: Sullivan currently works for the Alera Group and previously for Rich and Cartmill, the website states.
paras.zh: 该网站称，沙利文目前在 Alera Group 工作，此前曾在 Rich 和 Cartmill 工作。

paras.en: “Bob has seen carriers pull out of Oklahoma, leaving entire industries with one option and homeowners forced to pay more—or go without,” the website states. “He’s running to restore competition, cut costs, and deliver fast, fair claims for the people who actually pay the premiums.”
paras.zh: 该网站称：“鲍勃看到运营商撤出俄克拉荷马州，让整个行业只有一种选择，而房主被迫支付更多费用，或者放弃。” “他竞选的目的是恢复竞争、削减成本，并为实际支付保费的人提供快速、公平的索赔。”

paras.en: It adds that Sullivan “won’t take orders from the insurance lobbyist or career politicians. He’ll call out the price-gouging, expose slow-walking of claims and make insurance fair again for Oklahoma families and small businesses.”
paras.zh: 它还补充说，沙利文“不会听从保险游说者或职业政客的命令。他将谴责哄抬物价行为，揭露索赔进展缓慢，并使保险业再次对俄克拉荷马州家庭和小企业公平。”

paras.en: The website continues by saying that Sullivan will fight for transparency, lower rates and accountability.
paras.zh: 该网站还表示，沙利文将争取透明度、降低费率和问责制。

paras.en: MacIntyre has worked in the insurance industry for more than 30 years, according to his campaign website. This includes working as an actuary, product manager, underwriting and claims oversight, risk management, reserving, policy writing, state filings, legislative initiatives and consulting on new insurance legislation.
paras.zh: 据麦金泰尔的竞选网站称，麦金泰尔已在保险行业工作了 30 多年。这包括担任精算师、产品经理、承保和索赔监督、风险管理、准备金、保单撰写、国家备案、立法倡议和新保险立法咨询。

paras.en: His previous insurance work on his linkedIn includes roles at MacIntyre Holdings, an insurance consulting service, Home State Insurance Group and Old American County Mutual Fire Insurance Company.
paras.zh: 他之前在 LinkedIn 上的保险工作包括保险咨询服务公司 MacIntyre Holdings、Home State Insurance Group 和 Old American County Mutual Fire Insurance Company 的职位。

paras.en: MacIntrye says on his site that Oklahomans deserve affordable insurance rates, acceptable and fair claims practices and available insurance.
paras.zh: 麦金特里在他的网站上表示，俄克拉荷马人应该享有负担得起的保险费率、可接受且公平的索赔做法以及可用的保险。

paras.en: “The Consumer Protection Division of the OID will be given new authority to track and initiate exams when there is a pattern of unfair claims practices reported,” the website states. “No longer will complaints just get a letter from the OID.”
paras.zh: 该网站称：“OID 的消费者保护部门将获得新的权力，可以在发现不公平索赔行为的情况下进行跟踪和发起检查。” “投诉不再只是收到 OID 的一封信。”

paras.en: The website also states that MacIntyre will strengthen fraud investigations and meet with legislators to make meditation mandatory if requested by either party.
paras.zh: 该网站还表示，麦金泰尔将加强欺诈调查，并与立法者会面，如果任何一方要求，强制冥想。

paras.en: “I will be available to the policyholders of Oklahoma,” MacIntyre said. “I want to hear from you. The Insurance Commissioner is an Advocate for the four million people who live in Oklahoma. I will have your back and work every day to improve insurance in Oklahoma.”
paras.zh: “我将为俄克拉荷马州的保单持有人提供服务，”麦金泰尔说。 “我想听听您的意见。保险专员是俄克拉荷马州 400 万人的代言人。我会支持您，每天努力改善俄克拉荷马州的保险。”

paras.en: Insurify found that Oklahoma, California and Georgia are the states where policyholders are more likely to feel the influence of a news insurance commissioner on their home insurance premiums.
paras.zh: Insurify 发现，在俄克拉荷马州、加利福尼亚州和佐治亚州，保单持有人更有可能感受到新闻保险专员对其家庭保险费的影响。

paras.en: It found that since 2023, Oklahoma’s average home insurance premiums have increased by 38% and the next elected commissioner will be the first to exercise a new authority to reject excessive rate increases.
paras.zh: 报告发现，自 2023 年以来，俄克拉荷马州的平均房屋保险保费上涨了 38%，下一届当选的专员将首先行使新的权力，拒绝过度加息。
